title: get_hla_by_phenotype tool description names a column that endpoint does not return
description:
Found by review of genetics-results-suite-4h6.25 on 2026-08-07.

tools/definitions.py:1278 tells the model, for get_hla_by_phenotype: "Read `mlogp`, NOT `pval`".

The advice is right in spirit - that endpoint has no pval column and the guidance exists to stop the model inventing one - but the spelling is wrong for this branch. get_hla_by_phenotype goes to results-api /v1/hla/{resource}, whose _HLA_HEADER_SCHEMA (genetics-results-api/app/routers/hla.py:39) spells it mlog10p. It is get_hla_by_ALLELE, which reads hla_associations_v, that spells it mlogp.

So the description points the model at a column that does not exist in the payload it is describing.

This is what makes genetics-results-suite-5wm bite: a model primed on this description writes pl.col('mlogp') against the phenotype= branch of the SDK's hla() and gets ColumnNotFoundError.

NOT fixed inside genetics-results-suite-4h6.25: it edits a live MCP tool description, and per CLAUDE.md changes unrelated to the task at hand get asked about first. It is a one-word fix.

Fix alongside genetics-results-suite-5wm - if that bead decides to harmonise the SDK's column names, the right spelling here depends on which way it goes.
close_reason:
Landed as mcp 3da9f43, alongside genetics-results-suite-5wm (batched - same files, same defect class).

IT WAS TWO SITES, NOT ONE. The bead named the tool description. Grepping found the same wrong advice in src/genetics_mcp_server/config/defaults.py:77-81, the system prompt that is present in EVERY conversation. Fixing only definitions.py would have left the STRONGER signal telling the model to rank HLA results on `pval` - the tool description is read once when the tool is considered, the system prompt is always in context.

Both now say to rank on mlog10p. definitions.py:1278 (get_hla_by_phenotype) and :1310 (get_hla_by_allele, "Ranked by mlog10p"), plus the system prompt line.

Why the advice was actively harmful rather than merely stale: the HLA tools do not return `pval` in a form the model can rank on usefully, and a model told to rank on pval either invents the column or sorts the wrong direction - mlog10p sorts DESC for significance where pval sorts ASC. So the failure mode was silently inverted rankings, not an error.

VERIFIED no straggler: grepping src/ for mlogp now returns only min_mlogp occurrences, which are correct - min_mlogp is a tool PARAMETER and part of the public input schema, deliberately untouched. Its description at definitions.py:1317-1320 wisely names no column at all.

Batched with 5wm because 5wm renamed the very column this advice should point at; doing them separately would have meant two passes over definitions.py and defaults.py with a window where the advice named a column that did not exist yet.

Tests: mcp 1297 passed / 74 deselected (unchanged).

NOT APPLIED to any cluster - the system prompt ships in the mcp-server image and the tool descriptions with it, so this reaches users only at the next build/rollout, which is covered by 5wm's rollout section.

title: sync-datasets.sh resolves sibling repos from the repo root, so it silently skips when run from a worktree
description:
Found 2026-08-07 while fixing genetics-results-suite-bnb. Out of that bead's scope, left alone, but it will bite the next person.

scripts/sync-datasets.sh copies the canonical configs/datasets.yaml into the sibling service repos for local dev. It resolves them relative to the repo root as ../genetics-results-db, ../genetics-mcp-server and so on.

Run from a git worktree the repo root is <repo>/.claude/worktrees/<name>, so those relative paths point outside the tree entirely and resolve to nothing. The script WARNS and SKIPS rather than failing, so the sync silently does not happen.

Consequence seen for real: the genetics-results-db worktree's local datasets.yaml (gitignored, generated) predated master's HLA commit and had metadata for 14 of 15 views, missing hla_associations_v entirely. Anything reading it - including the API at startup, which raises without it - would have been working from a stale registry. The agent had to copy the canonical file by hand.

This matters more now that the epic runs in worktrees across three repos, and deploy.sh calls sync-datasets.sh best-effort before building the ConfigMap, so a stale copy can reach a deployment.

FIX: resolve the sibling paths from the git COMMON dir rather than the working tree - git rev-parse --git-common-dir gives the main checkout's .git even from a worktree, so its parent is the real repo root. Or resolve via git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree / an explicit SUITE_ROOT env var. Whichever is chosen, make a failed sibling resolution LOUD rather than a warn-and-skip: a silent no-op sync is how a stale registry reaches a deployment.
close_reason:
Landed as suite cdc044f. Batched with genetics-results-suite-6o3 (same defect class).

PREMISE CONFIRMED AND WORSE THAN WRITTEN. The bead said the script warns and skips from a worktree. It does - but MEASURED in a throwaway layout, if a directory of a sibling's name happens to exist BESIDE THE WORKTREE, the old script COPIES THE CANONICAL FILE INTO IT while the real sibling stays stale. Both halves in one run: `WARN: repo not found, skipping .../wt/../genetics-results-api` AND `OK: copied to .../wt/../genetics-results-db/configs/datasets.yaml` (the decoy), with both real siblings left at 14 views and no hla_associations_v.
HONEST QUALIFICATION, since I overstated this once: that requires a worktree literally named `genetics-results-db` under .claude/worktrees/, and none exists (only db-only-architecture). It is a demonstrated CAPABILITY of the naive relative path, not an observed event. check-worktree-paths.sh had flagged this inverse case as undetected; it is now impossible rather than undetected.

FIX: siblings resolve from `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, absolutised with cd+pwd before dirname. That absolutisation is the actual bug at the heart of this - with -C, a relative answer is relative to THAT directory, so it must be absolutised there or the result is garbage from any subdirectory. Same incantation install-git-hooks.sh (rxw) needed.

FAILURE MODES SPLIT, so that "loud" does not mean "breaks the deploy":
  sibling not checked out on this machine  -> SKIP,  exit 0
  sibling root unresolvable                -> ERROR, exit 1
  directory of the right name, wrong repo  -> ERROR, exit 1, other siblings still sync
Verified by REPRODUCTION rather than by reading that this cannot fail a deploy: deploy.sh:338-341 invokes it as `... || echo "WARN: ... (continuing)"`, and under set -euo pipefail errexit is suppressed on the left of ||, no pipeline is involved so pipefail is irrelevant, and the list's status is echo's 0. Lab: script exits 1 -> WARN printed -> deploy continued, rc=0.
The wrong-repo check reads pyproject.toml's name. First version used `grep -q "^name = \"$sib\""`, which is formatter-brittle - a TOML reformat, single quotes or removed spaces would turn a working sync into exit 1. Now tolerant of spacing and quote style but still anchored on the closing quote, so genetics-results-db-fork is still rejected. Verified both directions. It passes for every real sibling today (both have `name = "<repo>"` on line 2), so this was prevention, not repair.
SUITE_SIBLING_ROOT added for layouts where .git does not sit beside the repo root.

check-worktree-paths.sh (0xs) loses its sync-datasets case - nothing left to detect once the script resolves correctly - and now covers three. The count in project-spec was corrected: it said "one preflight for all four" four lines below a table row saying it no longer checks the fourth.

ALSO CORRECTED, a false claim in THREE places: the sibling configs/datasets.yaml copies are described as "committed". MEASURED FALSE - gitignored in both siblings (genetics-results-api/.gitignore:186, genetics-results-db/.gitignore:39, both under a comment saying they are synced from here) and `git ls-files configs/` returns nothing. deploy.sh's comment additionally justified the sync as preventing drift in copies "baked into freshly built images", which is IMPOSSIBLE - build.sh clones from GitHub, so a gitignored file cannot reach an image. datasets-yaml-schema.md's section was written PRESCRIPTIVELY ("should be committed ... lets CI compare"), so rather than silently deleting an intent it now records that committing them for a CI drift check was intended, never implemented, and would first require these repos to have CI at all - verified there are no .github/workflows in either sibling, and the only CI in the suite is genetics-results-browser's, which runs no drift check.

TESTED ONLY IN A THROWAWAY LAYOUT - the script writes into sibling checkouts, so it was never run against the real repos. Seven cases covered: old-from-worktree (the decoy write), new-from-worktree, new-from-main-checkout, sibling absent, wrong-repo directory, non-git copy, and SUITE_SIBLING_ROOT.

title: genetics SDK does not cover the HLA tools
description:
Found 2026-08-07 after merging master into the epic worktrees.

Master added get_hla_by_phenotype and get_hla_by_allele (genetics-mcp-server commit c8d8aa3, with tests/test_hla_tools.py). The genetics SDK built by genetics-results-suite-4h6.11 predates them, so its 17 functions cover 42 of the now-44 api-category tools.

That matters beyond completeness: the SDK is the surface a sandboxed script gets, so anything missing from it is unreachable from the code-execution arm. A benchmark comparing that arm against the full MCP tool surface would score it as unable to answer HLA questions - a measurement artefact, not a real difference.

FIX: add an hla() function collapsing both tools the way every other product does, with the shape as an argument: hla(phenotype=...) and hla(allele=...), exactly-one-selector enforced by the existing _one_of, and _reject on any argument the chosen branch cannot honour.

Follow the conventions .11 established and its review found necessary:
- percent-encode every caller-controlled URL path segment via _seg (61 were unencoded before; httpx normalises ../ so an unencoded segment reaches arbitrary endpoints with the internal bearer attached)
- return polars.DataFrame, raise GeneticsError rather than returning {'success': False}
- preserve column names on an empty result so a script filtering a no-hit phenotype does not hit ColumnNotFound
- raise on truncation rather than returning a silent prefix
- if it goes through db-api rather than results-api, carry columns through and build the frame from them: db-api returns rows POSITIONALLY, which is what produced transposed stringified frames on five other paths

Check first WHICH backend the two tools use - results-api (commit 21034cf added an /hla endpoint) or BigQuery (hla_associations_v exists) - and follow the matching precedent. Also check whether the trait column spelling ('phenotype', a third convention) needs surfacing in the SDK's docstring.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-mcp-server 5d0ac78. 1223 -> 1244 passed, 74 deselected, ruff check clean. Reviewed + fix round + re-verification; no blocking findings survived.

WHAT LANDED: sdk/client.py gains hla() with _one_of(phenotype=, allele=) and per-branch _reject (genes refused on allele=; min_mlogp/min_info/limit refused on phenotype=). min_* default to None and are substituted in-branch so min_info=0, which meaningfully DISABLES the imputation filter, is forwarded rather than eaten. SDK coverage of api-category tools goes 40/44 (see below - it was never going to be 44).

TICKET PREMISE CORRECTED - it asked WHICH backend the two tools use and assumed one answer. It is BOTH, ONE EACH: get_hla_by_phenotype -> results-api /v1/hla/{resource}; get_hla_by_allele -> BigQuery hla_associations_v. The per-phenotype tabix files cannot span 2,712 phenotypes, so the reverse question has no file to read. This is the only SDK collapse whose branches read different stores, so the db-api positional-rows guidance applied to the allele= branch only.

CONSEQUENCE THE TICKET MISSED: the two branches return DIFFERENT COLUMN NAMES for the same quantities - results-api mlog10p/se/af/af_cases/af_controls vs the view's mlogp/sebeta/af_alt/af_alt_cases/af_alt_controls. Both spellings verified against the real schemas (genetics-results-api/app/routers/hla.py:30 and configs/datasets.yaml:831), not inferred. Kept as ONE function and documented rather than renamed: harmonising asserts the two backends' quantities are semantically identical, which needs checking against the munge code, not assuming from the name. Filed as genetics-results-suite-5wm and made a blocker of .23, since it biases the code-execution arm's iteration count.

TWO FINDINGS I ESCALATED ABOVE THE REVIEWER'S NIT LABEL AND FIXED:
1. resource was the ONE caller-controlled SQL literal in executor.py not passed through quote_literal (line ~1439), and /v1/hla/{resource} was the one unencoded URL path segment (that endpoint landed in c8d8aa3, after the _seg sweep). The reviewer rated it NIT because db-api restricts to read-only SELECT anyway. Escalated because this epic's entire purpose is to put prompt-injectable LLM-authored strings into these arguments, and get_hla_by_allele is the exact method this task modified. Also moved LIMIT {int(max_rows)} to sql_int(maximum=_MAX_SQL_LIMIT), which was safe only because query_database happens to strip the trailing LIMIT.
   Verified: 11 hostile resource values and 6 bad max_rows values reach the SQL builder ZERO times (counted awaits, not assert_not_awaited), and surface to a script as GeneticsError rather than an empty frame, because GeneticsClient._payload raises on success=False. MAX_ROWS renders LIMIT 100000, exactly sql_int's inclusive maximum - no off-by-one that would make every default SDK call fail.
   37 real resource ids validated against the allow-list, zero rejected. The load-bearing argument is not the enumeration though: four other executor paths ALREADY gate resource names through quote_literal, so a live name this rejects would already be breaking asm_qtl, open_chromatin, mpra and mpra_pip_concordance.
2. docs/project-spec.md claimed the SDK replaces '42 API-category tools'. Re-derived from TOOL_DEFINITIONS: 44 exist, SDK reaches 40. Per CLAUDE.md's counts-rot-silently rule this belonged in the same commit.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE TICKET TEXT: an empty result on the phenotype= branch does NOT retain its schema (verified: ColumnNotFoundError). The ticket required preserving column names on empty results. results-api returns rows with no schema to recover names from, and the only fix available here was hardcoding its 15-column schema across a repo boundary where it rots silently - a worse failure than the one it prevents. SDK-wide, not introduced here. Filed as genetics-results-suite-6uk with three real fix options. The BigQuery-backed branches DO honour it, because db-api derives columns from the BigQuery job schema, which is populated even for a zero-row result.

MCP OUTPUT UNCHANGED, as the epic requires: get_hla_by_allele gained with_metadata: bool = False routed through _query_metadata so columns/truncated reach the SDK. definitions.py:2274 passes five positional args, so nothing in the tool surface can set it. Default-path payload keys verified byte-identical, pinned by a test in both directions.

LEFT UNDONE ON PURPOSE, both from c8d8aa3 landing beside 45c729e rather than through it, both changing live MCP output which this epic forbids until the profile flips:
- genetics-results-suite-buc (P1): get_hla_by_allele hands the model unlabelled positional lists. Confirmed empirically - results[0] == ['K11_COELIAC','HLA-DQB1','DQB1*02:01',1596.65,...] with no columns key. Exactly the defect bef fixed for the by-gene tools. Also needs the _download_data hole checked.
- genetics-results-suite-84o (P2): get_hla_by_phenotype's description says 'Read mlogp' while that endpoint returns mlog10p. One word, but it is what makes 5wm bite.

ALSO FILED: 5zz (SDK covers 40/44 - resolved per-tool during review; only get_myvariant_annotations is genuinely unreachable data, so the remaining decision is one tool not four, and it belongs to .23 rather than the SDK), bi1 (batched nits: raw-vs-normalized resource echo, two doc redundancies, the ruff-format drift on executor.py).

ENVIRONMENT: the 6o3 trap bit again and is now confirmed as a standing hazard in this repo - the editable install points at the MAIN CHECKOUT, so bare python/pytest in a worktree imports genetics_mcp_server from /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-mcp-server/src, which has no _seg at all. Only the worktree's own .venv/bin/python resolves correctly. The test-runner agent correctly refused to proceed on this. Every number above was produced by an agent that asserted the resolved path first.

title: Agents dispatched into a sibling repo cannot read this beads database
description:
Orchestration defect found 2026-08-07 while fixing genetics-results-suite-bef. The fix agent flagged it; earlier agents did not.

Each repo in the suite has its OWN beads workspace. Verified:
  genetics-results-suite/.beads   -> 179 issues (this epic lives here)
  genetics-mcp-server/.beads      -> 127 issues
  genetics-results-db/.beads      -> 7 issues

bd resolves the workspace from the working directory. So an agent working in /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-mcp-server/.claude/worktrees/... running 'bd show genetics-results-suite-4h6.1' gets 'no issue found matching'.

Every implementation and review agent dispatched into the mcp-server or db worktrees during this epic was instructed to 'bd show <bead> and read its notes field'. None of them could. Only the last one said so.

IMPACT WAS CONTAINED because every prompt restated the task detail inline - which is why the work came out correct. But it means:
- the notes fields written as durable cross-task handoffs (e.g. .4's 'secret=true now also means no metrics row', .19's user authorization and constraints) reached agents only because they were repeated in the prompt, not because they were read
- an agent could silently proceed without the context it was told to fetch, and several did without flagging it

FIX, pick one:
(a) Orchestrator stops telling cross-repo agents to run bd, and always inlines the bead text and notes. Simple, works today, but the notes stop being a durable channel and become prompt-authoring discipline.
(b) Give agents the suite path explicitly: 'run bd from /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-results-suite'. bd would then resolve the right workspace.
(c) Consolidate: track cross-repo epics in one workspace and reference it from the others.

Also worth deciding: the sibling repos' beads databases (127 and 7 issues) are separate backlogs that this epic has been ignoring. Check whether anything in them conflicts with or duplicates the epic's work.
notes:
--- CORRECTION, appended after closing ---
THIS BEAD'S CLOSE REASON SAYS THE SIBLING BACKLOGS ARE ENTIRELY CLOSED. THAT IS TRUE ONLY OF THE TWO REPOS I ACTUALLY CHECKED. I measured genetics-mcp-server (127 total / 0 open) and genetics-results-db (7 total / 0 open) and then generalised to "the siblings", which was exactly the unchecked-assertion failure this epic keeps hitting. genetics-results-browser ALSO HAS A BEADS STORE - discovered incidentally when committing genetics-results-suite-n3p, because its pre-commit hook printed "Exported 79 issues".
genetics-results-browser: 79 total, 75 closed, **4 OPEN**, 4 ready, 0 blocked:
- genetics-results-browser-3lu (P1 epic) speed up /v1/results network requests, GCS-seek bottleneck; child .4 tune CHUNK_SIZE (100) and FANOUT_CONCURRENCY (8)
- genetics-results-browser-6va (P2 bug) admin sessions API can return null created_at/updated_at
- genetics-results-browser-fyd (P3) genetics-mcp-server: admin API emits naive (offset-less) UTC timestamps
THE OPERATIONAL CONCLUSION SURVIVES: none of the four touches the 4h6 code-execution epic - they are results-api transfer performance and admin-API timestamp hygiene - so there is still no conflict or duplication to reconcile. But the STATED BASIS was wrong, and `fyd` is itself an instance of this bead's subject: an issue about genetics-mcp-server filed in the browser's store, where nobody working the mcp repo would ever see it.
The skill's "check sibling backlogs once per epic" rule is hereby scoped to ALL FIVE sibling repos named in the suite CLAUDE.md cross-repo section (genetics-results-api, -db, -browser, -munge, genetics-mcp-server), not to whichever ones a task happened to touch. Enumerate from CLAUDE.md, do not enumerate from memory.
close_reason:
PREMISE RE-VERIFIED AS TRUE, mechanism established, and BOTH open questions answered. No code change - this is an orchestration defect, and the fix landed in the orchestrator's own operating instructions (the beads-ralph-wiggum skill), which is the only place that can act on it.

MEASURED TODAY, not assumed. `bd show genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 --json` fails identically from ALL FOUR sibling locations - the mcp-server and results-db worktrees AND both plain checkouts - with `no issue found matching`. Control in both directions: the same id resolves fully from the suite worktree, and `bd show genetics-mcp-server-1` from the mcp worktree returns an ambiguous-id error listing 21 mcp issues, proving that location is talking to its own store and only its own store.

MECHANISM, measured rather than guessed: bd walks up from the CWD to the nearest .beads/ and that directory's repo owns the store. No BEADS_* env var exists; neither ~/.beads nor ~/.config/beads exists; all three config.yaml files are stock templates with every line commented out, INCLUDING the experimental multi-repo `repos: primary/additional` hydration block - so nothing cross-hydrates. Sibling WORKTREES carry only the git-tracked subset (config.yaml, issues.jsonl, metadata.json, hooks) with no embeddeddolt/, and resolve through to their own repo's main checkout store. `bd doctor` is unavailable in embedded mode, which itself confirms the mode.

WHY IT LOOKED FINE ALL SESSION, which is the part worth keeping: a subagent's shell cwd RESETS to the session's own worktree between bash calls. An agent that edits sibling-repo files BY ABSOLUTE PATH therefore never leaves the suite workspace and its bd calls resolve normally. The failure only bites when an agent `cd`s into the sibling first. That is why this session's cross-repo agents appeared to read beads successfully while the bead says they cannot - both are true, under different command shapes. (The cwd-reset explanation is inference about those agents' commands; the four failure measurements are direct.)

FIX ADOPTED: essentially (b), but sharpened by the mechanism above and written into the beads-ralph-wiggum skill as a standing rule rather than left as a one-off:
- every prompt that names a bead and targets another repo must state where bd resolves ("bd only resolves <prefix>-* ids when your cwd is inside <orchestrating worktree>; it fails from this repo's worktree");
- notes are the DURABLE RECORD, never the TRANSPORT - anything an agent must act on gets inlined;
- agents are told to REPORT a bd failure rather than proceed, because silent proceeding is the actual defect (only one agent in the whole epic said so);
- sibling backlogs get checked once per epic.
(a) was rejected as the primary answer because it abandons notes as a channel entirely; (c), consolidating into one workspace, is a bigger change than the problem warrants now that the mechanism is understood and the sibling backlogs turn out to be empty.

THE BEAD'S SECOND QUESTION IS ANSWERED AND THE ANSWER IS "NOTHING": it asked whether the sibling repos' backlogs conflict with or duplicate this epic's work. They cannot - `bd stats` today gives genetics-mcp-server 127 total / 0 OPEN and genetics-results-db 7 total / 0 OPEN. Both are entirely closed. There is no parallel backlog to reconcile.
Counts have moved since the bead was written (2026-08-07): it recorded 179 / 127 / 7. Siblings are unchanged; the suite store has grown 179 -> 262. Three distinct counts from three locations is itself the confirmation that these are three distinct workspaces.

IMPACT ASSESSMENT UNCHANGED AND STILL CORRECT: the work came out right because every prompt restated the task detail inline. That was luck backed by prompt discipline, not a working channel, and the skill change converts it into a stated rule.

title: usage SSE chunk folds cache reads and creations together, so cost cannot be computed exactly
description:
Found building the replay harness (genetics-results-suite-4h6.4) on 2026-08-07. Small change, disproportionate value.

llm_service.py emits a per-iteration 'usage' StreamChunk carrying iteration, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_input_tokens, total_output_tokens, context_window, context_percent.

TWO PROBLEMS for anything measuring cost off the stream:

1. The chunk's input_tokens is NOT the billed input. llm_service.py ~786 sets it to input_tok + cache_read + cache_create - i.e. the whole context - while total_input_tokens accumulates only raw input_tok. Anyone reading input_tokens as billed input overstates it, badly, on a cache-heavy turn.

2. Cache READS and cache CREATIONS are folded into that single number and never separated. They differ by more than 12x in price (Opus: ~0.50 vs ~6.25 per M tokens). So an exact USD figure cannot be derived from the stream at all.

The replay harness works around (2) by reporting an INTERVAL - cost_usd_min pricing all cached tokens as reads, cost_usd_max pricing them all as creations - rather than fabricating a single number. That is honest but it weakens the primary metric that genetics-results-suite-4h6.23 gates the whole code-execution rollout on. Production data shows the cache-read share swinging 11% -> 52% across a turn's iterations, so the interval will not be narrow.

FIX: add cache_read and cache_create to the usage StreamChunk payload in llm_service.py. Both values are already computed and logged one line above (the 'API call iteration=' log line carries cache_read= and cache_create=), so this is exposing what already exists, not new instrumentation. Then the harness can compute exact cost and drop the interval.

Note chat_turn_metrics (task .1) DOES store cache_read_tokens and cache_create_tokens separately - but the benchmark runs with secret=true, which writes no row, which is why it reads the stream instead. This is the gap between those two paths.
close_reason:
Landed as mcp 0bff88a + browser 479642b. FULL tier - implementation, sighted review + blind validator in parallel, one fix round. mcp suite 1370 -> 1372 passed / 74 deselected (+2 = exactly the new tests). browser `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.

WHAT LANDED: `cache_read` and `cache_create` are emitted alongside `input_tokens` on the usage StreamChunk, read off the SAME `message.usage` in the same iteration. Billed input is `input_tokens - cache_read - cache_create`.

`input_tokens` KEEPS ITS MEANING - the whole per-iteration context, cached and uncached - and this was the bead's real decision. The consumer survey settled it decisively and not on my reasoning: LLMChat.tsx:1125-1139 renders `input_tokens` against `context_window` AS THE CONTEXT METER. Redefining it to billed input would have made that bar under-report by the entire cached amount and visibly disagree with the `context_percent` figure printed beside it. So the two components are ADDED, never substituted. Do not "simplify" this later by redefining the field.

THE ARITHMETIC WAS PROVEN, NOT REVIEWED. Both validators attacked the cost identity independently and both cleared it. The blind one did it by RUNNING hand-built fakes through the real `_stream_anthropic` loop rather than reading the diff: a provider with no cache attributes at all yields 0/0 correctly; a `max_tokens` continuation yields two chunks with iteration 1->2 and cost-from-stream equal to the recorded row; a retried request (first `messages.stream()` raising APIConnectionError) yields exactly ONE usage chunk carrying only the successful attempt's numbers, no stale or duplicated values; and a two-iteration tool turn priced by hand against Opus-5 rates gave 0.04825 from the stream == 0.04825 hand-computed == 0.04825 recorded. The sighted reviewer independently established that an off-by-one across iterations is STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE: `message` comes from `get_final_message()` inside the retry loop which either breaks on success or raises, so it never falls through stale, and the yield is straight-line from the read with no branch between.

THE DIFF'S OWN DOC CLAIM WAS FALSE AND WAS FIXED IN-CYCLE. I wrote "a consumer can therefore price a turn exactly from the stream alone". Both validators falsified it independently, on four axes, and the fix agent re-verified all four against the code before rewriting:
- SUBAGENT CALLS. subagent.py:261-266 issues its own messages.create with private counters. `total_cost` in llm_service.py is touched at exactly two places, :797 (= 0.0) and :877 (+= iter_cost), and nothing from the subagent path (:1016, :1233) feeds it - while :1184 writes total_cost into the metrics row. So a turn calling launch_subagents costs strictly more than EITHER source reports.
- RETRIED ATTEMPTS. :845-868 retries in place on APIConnectionError / 500 / 502 / 503 / 529; `message.usage` is read only at :871, after the break. Tokens burned by abandoned attempts are billed and invisible.
- THE OPENAI PATH EMITS NO USAGE CHUNK AT ALL. _stream_openai (:601-654) yields text and `done` only. Pre-existing, and replay_benchmark.py already handles it with a `no_usage_chunks` status rather than a zero - so the whole section is Anthropic-path-only.
- THE STREAM CARRIES NO MODEL NAME, and cost.py's _match_pricing falls back to claude-sonnet for anything unrecognised. The consumer must be told the model out-of-band.
The doc now states the accurate claim - the stream prices THE MAIN AGENTIC LOOP'S ANTHROPIC CALLS exactly, given the model - and names all four exclusions, noting that the first two sit outside the chat_turn_metrics row as well, so THE STREAM AND THE ROW AGREE WITH EACH OTHER WHILE BOTH UNDERSTATE WHAT WAS BILLED. That is the trap worth knowing about.

THE NEW TEST'S DOCSTRING RECORDS WHY IT PASSES. `test_the_stream_alone_reproduces_the_recorded_cost` recomputes cost from the emitted payload fields and compares to chat_turn_metrics.cost_usd - a genuinely different route to the same number, so it catches a dropped/renamed field (KeyError), reads and creations swapped or merged (the 12.5x price gap moves the sum), and `input_tokens` silently redefined to billed input (the subtraction goes negative). But it passes BECAUSE BOTH SIDES SHARE THE BLIND SPOTS ABOVE. It validates the payload arithmetic, NOT the completeness of the accounting, and now says so. Assertions unchanged.

BROWSER FIELDS ARE OPTIONAL, DELIBERATELY. The first draft declared them required. The browser deploys independently of the MCP backend, so during a rollout window it can legitimately receive usage events predating this change; required would assert a guarantee the wire does not make. Zero runtime impact either way - nothing constructs a ContextUsage literal, the sole site is a cast at LLMChat.tsx:772.

ALSO FIXED, pre-existing: `context_percent` was documented as total_input_tokens / context_window. The code has always used the full per-iteration context.

DELIBERATELY LEFT UNDONE, and this is why the harness still shows an interval: IterationUsage (scripts/replay_benchmark.py:90-101) was NOT extended, so iterations_detail still omits both new fields and replay_benchmark.py:307 still computes the min/max interval. Switching the harness over is genetics-results-suite-4h6.4's work, and the doc says so explicitly. The producer side is now unblocked; nothing consumes it yet.
Frontend likewise consumes nothing new - LLMChat.tsx renders only context_percent/input_tokens/context_window, and its `data.input_tokens >= prev.input_tokens` guard at :772 keeps only one event, so cost is not derivable frontend-side despite the widened type. That is fine; the benchmark is the intended consumer.

title: Worktree venv trap: uv run resolves to the pyenv shim and tests the main checkout
description:
Discovered 2026-08-07 while implementing genetics-results-suite-4h6.1.

In a freshly created git worktree of genetics-mcp-server, 'uv run pytest' resolved to the PYENV SHIM (/home/jkarjala/.pyenv/shims/pytest) rather than the worktree's own venv — pytest was never installed in the worktree .venv. That global interpreter imports genetics_mcp_server from the MAIN CHECKOUT at /home/jkarjala/suite/genetics-mcp-server/src.

Consequence: a test run in the worktree silently exercises MAIN CHECKOUT source against WORKTREE tests. Edits made in the worktree are invisible, and the run reports green. The baseline established this way (977 passed) happened to be numerically correct only because both trees were at the same clean commit b2a1df4 — had the main checkout been dirty, every result would have been meaningless.

FIX for any agent working in a genetics-mcp-server worktree:
1. Run 'uv sync --extra dev' in the worktree (installs the declared dev extra into the existing venv; does not create a new one).
2. ASSERT resolution before trusting any result:
     uv run python -c "import genetics_mcp_server, sys; print(genetics_mcp_server.__file__); print(sys.executable)"
   Both paths must be under the worktree.

Corrected baseline after the fix: 977 passed, 74 deselected, 0 failed (~150s), verified under two pytest-randomly seeds. pytest-randomly 4.1.0 IS installed and active, so the suite is genuinely shuffled and order dependence is tested.

Worth considering whether to make this fail loudly rather than relying on every agent remembering — e.g. a conftest.py assertion that the imported package path is under the rootdir.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-mcp-server 91349bf, genetics-results-api 0c63ce7, genetics-results-db a79c816. Batched with genetics-results-suite-e47.

The bead's own suggestion - "a conftest.py assertion that the imported package path is under the rootdir" - implemented in all three python repos. It raises pytest.UsageError from pytest_configure, so the run aborts BEFORE COLLECTION rather than surfacing as a buried test failure, and the message names both resolved paths plus the fix.

THE THREE REPOS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC, AND ASSUMING THEY WERE WOULD HAVE SHIPPED THE WRONG GUARD IN TWO OF THEM. Install modes established empirically, not assumed:
  genetics-mcp-server   EDITABLE install (.venv/.../_editable_impl_genetics_mcp_server.pth points at one tree's src/). A foreign interpreter imports a foreign tree - the exact trap. Guard compares the package's __file__ against rootdir.
  genetics-results-api  NOT installed; `app` is a NAMESPACE package
  genetics-results-db   NOT installed, no [build-system] at all; `api` is a namespace package
For the latter two __file__ IS None (verified: app.__file__ is None, type(app.__path__) is _NamespacePath), so the mcp-shaped assertion would have been LITERALLY INAPPLICABLE. They compare every __path__ entry instead.

THAT ASYMMETRY SURFACED A REAL, CURRENTLY-SILENT LEAK in the two namespace repos, and it is the more valuable finding here. Namespace packages MERGE every matching sys.path entry, so PYTHONPATH pointing at the main checkout adds its app/ to __path__ alongside the worktree's. MEASURED: app.__path__ ends up [<worktree>/app, <worktree>/app, <main checkout>/app]. A module present only in the main checkout imports from there, and a deletion made in the worktree is invisible. PYTHONPATH=<checkout> is exactly what a bare `python scripts/...` run needs in results-api, so this is reachable by ordinary use, not just by the pyenv-shim accident the bead described.

NO SPURIOUS FIRE, checked where it could plausibly happen rather than assumed: both sides of every comparison are Path(...).resolve(), so symlinks, trailing slashes, .. segments and /home-vs-realpath all normalise - there is no string comparison to attack. rootdir inference holds when running pytest from tests/ in api and db (all three repos have pyproject.toml at the root). And there is no CI, Dockerfile or tox/nox anywhere in the three repos that installs non-editable and then runs pytest, so no existing workflow trips it.
Guards proven to catch the REAL trap in all three: running the worktree's tests with the MAIN CHECKOUT's interpreter fired the mcp guard at configure with both paths named, exit 4, zero tests collected; PYTHONPATH=<main checkout> fired the api and db guards.
Suites unaffected: mcp 1360 passed / 74 deselected, api 236 passed offline, db 140 passed, --collect-only clean in all three.

KNOWN LIMIT, stated rather than papered over: _NamespacePath recomputes on sys.path change, so a conftest, plugin or test that mutates sys.path AFTER pytest_configure is not caught - measured, a post-import append does grow __path__. The realistic vector (PYTHONPATH) is present at configure time, so this is a documented boundary rather than a hole.
NIT LEFT: the mcp guard would abort a legitimate future "pip install . and test the installed wheel" workflow, and its message asserts unconditionally that the interpreter is not this tree's .venv, which would be wrong in that case. Nothing does that today.

STRAY FILE NOT COMMITTED: a uv.lock appeared untracked in the genetics-results-db worktree as a side effect of an agent running uv there. It is new (no git history) and was not part of this work, so it was deliberately left unstaged rather than swept into the commit. Decide whether that repo should have a lockfile on its own merits.

title: Backfill phenotype and dataset metadata into BigQuery
description:
Highest-leverage single backfill. Phenotype/trait metadata and the dataset registry exist today only as per-dataset metadata_file JSONs (datasets.yaml:1190+) plus the resources/profiles blocks, reachable only through results-api. That is why a phenotype question costs a search call, a lookup call and then the real query.

Load them as BigQuery tables (phenotypes, datasets) with a phenotype_v view, so trait-code resolution becomes a JOIN inside a single query rather than a separate roundtrip. Tens of thousands of rows - small.

This unlocks lookup_phenotype_names, get_resource_metadata, get_dataset_display_names, list_datasets and the FILTERING half of search_phenotypes. Fuzzy ranked search stays on results-api - BigQuery cannot replace it and it remains the entry point of most conversations.

Files: genetics-results-db/schemas/phenotypes.sql + phenotype_v.sql (new), scripts/load_phenotypes.sh (new), api/main.py VIEWS allowlist, configs/datasets.yaml, docs/adding-datasets.md.
notes:
USER DECISION 2026-08-07: authorized to run against production BigQuery. This work is ADDITIVE - it creates new tables and views and touches no existing data - which is why it is cleared ahead of .18.

Still required: dry-run every statement first and report estimated bytes before executing. Do not TRUNCATE or REPLACE anything that already exists.

Highest-leverage backfill in the epic: phenotype/trait metadata and the dataset registry exist today only as per-dataset metadata_file JSONs (configs/datasets.yaml:1190+) reachable through results-api, which is why a phenotype question currently costs a search call, a lookup call and then the real query. As BigQuery tables with a phenotype_v view, trait-code resolution becomes a JOIN inside a single query.

Phenotype and dataset metadata backfilled into production BigQuery. genetics-results-db worktree 52e9175, genetics-results-suite worktree d96a913. phenotypes 32,611 rows, datasets 888. 47 tests pass. One reviewer verified against production, one fix round.

ADDITIVE ONLY - review confirmed no TRUNCATE/DROP/ALTER/DELETE touched any of the 12 pre-existing tables; the loader writes WRITE_TRUNCATE to two new names and is idempotent.

TICKET FRAMING WRONG TWICE, both found by VERIFYING rather than reading:
1. The join key is trait_original, not trait. trait is a display string (Height,_inverse-rank_normalized); trait_original holds the phenocode (HEIGHT_IRN). The first table keyed on trait and joined ZERO rows SILENTLY. Verified live after the fix: FinnGen_R14 1380/1425, kanta 328/328, Open Targets 20312/20312, genebass 4501/4501 in both exome tables - and five datasets still go to zero on trait.
2. Neither resource nor the registry id can be the key - the relation to the results-view dataset value is many-to-many in BOTH directions (pgc_scz+pgc_bip inside PGC; genebass_exome+genebass_gene_based inside genebass; finngen_pqtl is FinnGen_Olink in credible_sets but FinnGen_Olink_3K in colocalization). That mapping exists in NO config - it is baked into munge-produced TSVs - so BQ_DATASETS_BY_DATASET_ID owns it.

CAUGHT IN REVIEW - the same silent-wrong-answer class, twice more:
- db-api /query auto-qualifier did a bare string replace. Adding two common English words to the allow-list corrupted string literals: a LIKE pattern containing the word datasets had the fully-qualified table name spliced into it, which RUNS and returns zero rows. authorize_query cannot catch it - the SQL is valid and touches only allowed tables. Renaming the table was REJECTED as the fix: it repairs one word and leaves phenotypes, variant_annotation, gene_annotations, open_chromatin. The replace now rewrites only FROM/JOIN positions. All 47 examples across all 14 views verified to still qualify AND dry-run clean. Known residual, documented and pinned by a test: FROM/JOIN inside a string literal is still rewritten.
- phenotypes.dataset_id was documented as joining datasets.dataset_id but resolved to NOTHING for every registry entry that lost a merge (388 kanta rows). Now labelled provenance, not a join key, naming the two ids that match nothing.
- The drift cross-check disabled ITSELF: a bq failure yielded an empty string that read as falsy, so validation was skipped and the load proceeded anyway. Now refuses unless ALLOW_UNVALIDATED=1.
- validate() was missing the mapped-minus-live direction. Added; found 7 registry entries in no results table (IIBDGC plus 6 QTD sub-studies). Suppressed deliberately via ABSENT_FROM_RESULTS with a reason each, emitted with dataset NULL, and SELF-EXPIRING - the build fails if a suppressed name goes live. All four checks are now fatal, not advisory; the previous advisory warning for IIBDGC had been emitted and ignored.

VERIFIED CORRECT BY REVIEW: schema NOT NULL choices against real data; unpartitioned plus clustered matching gene_annotations and peak_to_gene; the generate_resource_sql.py ALL_VIEWS and monitor/bq_summary.py exclusions, because their resource is a real registry column rather than a name-derived CASE so a coverage check would be circular; cross-repo docs complete in both repos; 0 duplicate keys in either table, joins 1:1 with no fan-out.

title: Materialize variant/resource as stored columns and re-cluster credible_sets
description:
Pure win, independent of which agent interface wins - do it regardless.

credible_sets_v derives BOTH variant and resource in the view (schemas/credible_sets_v.sql) while the base table clusters on dataset, data_type, gene_most_severe, most_severe (schemas/credible_sets.sql:26-27). So the two filters the agent is told to use prune NOTHING. datasets.yaml:237 already documents the workaround ('Always add the chr filter next to variant ... without it the same query scans ~20x more data').

Store variant and resource as real columns (variant_effect, mpra and variant_annotation already do this) and re-cluster to resource, data_type, trait, pos. pos and trait are not clustering keys today despite region and QTL-by-gene being dominant shapes.

Measure scan bytes before and after on the ten commonest queries from genetics_api_logs and record the numbers in the issue.

Files: genetics-results-db/schemas/credible_sets.sql, credible_sets_v.sql, scripts/setup_bigquery.sh.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-10. STOPPED at step 4 as authorized. Nothing existing modified - no DROP/ALTER/CREATE OR REPLACE ran, no repo file changed, credible_sets and credible_sets_v untouched.

TWO TICKET PREMISES FAILED.
(1) 'the ten commonest queries from genetics_api_logs' - that table does NOT record SQL. Its only log_type is endpoint_access and all 223k rows come from the FILE/TABIX api (genetics-results-api), which never touches BigQuery. The only place BigQuery SQL is logged is genetics_api_logs.stdout, whose jsonPayload carries sql/bytes_processed/dry_run: 538 rows over 2026-05-21..2026-08-10, 375 referencing credible_sets_v. Small and agent/MCP-dominated - state that whenever these numbers are cited.
(2) 'QTL-by-gene is a dominant shape' is NOT supported. trait equality is 19.2%, and HALF of all trait filtering is LIKE '%..%', which no clustering can prune.

REAL FILTER FREQUENCY over 375 queries: data_type 52.5%, resource 46.7%, chr 30.1%, pos 29.1%, trait/trait_original equality 19.2%, trait LIKE 19.2% (unprunable), variant 10.1% (36 of 38 WITHOUT a chr filter), gene_most_severe 6.1%, most_severe 4.8%, dataset 3.5%.
BYTE ATTRIBUTION: 96.5% of all bytes come from queries with NO chr filter - 67.3% 'other, no chr' plus 29.3% 'variant, no chr' (36 queries, 426 GB). Region queries are only 3.5% of bytes.

CORE PREMISE CONFIRMED BY MEASUREMENT: WHERE resource='finngen' on credible_sets_v scans 4,176,706,833 B versus 2,520,802,636 B unfiltered - MORE than unfiltered, because it must additionally read dataset to evaluate the CASE. Zero pruning. Meanwhile WHERE dataset='FinnGen_R14' (a real cluster key) prunes to 347,487,447 B. The datasets.yaml:237 11.5x variant/chr warning also confirmed exactly.

METHODOLOGY TRAP WORTH KEEPING: --dry_run is NOT usable for this comparison. On the live table dry-run equals actual, but on a freshly-created CTAS table the dry-run estimate IGNORES CLUSTERING until BigQuery's storage optimiser has processed it. Observed: resource+data_type dry-ran at 4,492,232,401 B and actually processed 517,406,337 B. A first benchmark pass using dry-run showed the new tables as uniformly WORSE - a pure artefact. All recorded numbers are real total_bytes_processed with use_query_cache=False. Measurement cost ~350-400 GB scanned, roughly USD 2-2.50.

THREE EXPERIMENT TABLES BUILT, all clearly non-live, all CREATE TABLE (no OR REPLACE), all with OPTIONS(description='EXPERIMENT genetics-results-suite-4h6.18 ... NOT LIVE. Safe to drop.'), all PARTITION BY RANGE_BUCKET(chr, GENERATE_ARRAY(1,23,1)), all 115,043,095 rows, all with stored variant and resource:
  credible_sets_exp_rdtp  resource, data_type, trait, pos    <- the ticket's proposal
  credible_sets_exp_rdvp  resource, data_type, variant, pos
  credible_sets_exp_drvp  data_type, resource, variant, pos

WEIGHTED TOTAL over the top-10 shapes, weighted by log frequency: before 333.14 GB; rdtp 47.00 GB (-85.9%); rdvp 43.48 GB (-86.9%); drvp 43.45 GB (-87.0%).

THE TICKET'S OWN KEY CHOICE IS THE WORST OF THE THREE, and it carries the only in-set regression: Q9 (region + data_type + trait LIKE) is +12.0% under rdtp and improves under both alternatives. And R5 (data_type='eQTL' AND trait='SORT1' - the QTL-by-gene shape the ticket names as its justification for putting trait in the key) gets essentially NOTHING under rdtp: -2.3%, because trait at position 3 is not on a filtered prefix when resource is omitted. drvp gives it -18.0%.

pos as key 4 is doing nothing measurable. rdvp/drvp match or beat rdtp on every region shape despite putting variant ahead of pos.

REGRESSIONS AGAINST THE OLD CLUSTER KEYS - real and material, weighted by how often those columns are filtered:
  dataset='FinnGen_R14' (old key 1, 3.5% of queries): 0.560 -> 1.559 rdtp (+178%) / 1.691 rdvp (+202%) / 2.053 drvp (+267%)
  gene_most_severe='SORT1' (old key 3, 6.1%):         6.161 -> 9.014 (+46%) / 8.854 (+44%) / 8.850 (+44%)
  most_severe IN (...) (old key 4, 4.8%):             9.509 -> 10.259 (+8%) all three
  no filter at all:                                   2.373 -> 1.971 (-17%) all three

SIZE DELTA +13.5% logical (23.74 -> 26.96 GB). Stored variant 1.96 GB, stored resource 1.25 GB. Both are CHEAPER TO READ THAN TO DERIVE - deriving variant needs chr+pos+ref+alt = 2.57 GB, deriving resource needs dataset = 1.66 GB - which is why the unfiltered scan got 17% BETTER despite the bigger table. Storage cost is negligible against the scan saving.

CROSS-REPO CONSEQUENCE, reported not changed: after this change the datasets.yaml:237 workaround ('always add the chr filter next to variant') becomes WRONG - adding chr goes from an 11.5x saving to marginally counterproductive (ratio 0.94-0.95x). That is the canonical configs/datasets.yaml in the SUITE repo and belongs to a different task.

WHY NO REPO FILE WAS TOUCHED: scripts/setup_bigquery.sh auto-creates a table for EVERY schemas/*.sql that is not *_v.sql, so adding a schema file would have created the experiment table on the next production setup run. Editing any of the three listed files IS the swap.

IMPLEMENTATION PATH FOR THE EVENTUAL SWAP: scripts/load_data.py already has the staging-table indirection (const_columns / convert_chr / strip_cell_type_prefix) used to project computed columns, so variant and resource can be materialised there without changing the source TSVs.

CLEANUP OWED once a decision is made: drop credible_sets_exp_rdtp, credible_sets_exp_rdvp, credible_sets_exp_drvp in phewas-development.genetics_results.

USER DECISION 2026-08-10: clustering is data_type, resource, variant, pos. Weighted total over the ten commonest logged shapes 333.14 GB to 43.45 GB, -87.0%.

THE TICKET'S OWN KEY ORDER WAS THE WORST OF THE THREE BENCHMARKED. Its stated justification for putting trait in the key was that QTL-by-gene is a dominant shape; measured, a QTL-by-gene query that omits resource gets -2.3% under that order because trait at position 3 is not on a filtered prefix, versus -18.0% under the chosen one. trait equality is only 19.2% of queries and half of all trait filtering is LIKE with leading wildcards, which no clustering can prune. The ticket's order also carried the only in-set regression, +12.0% on region plus trait LIKE.

THE TICKET WAS ALSO WRONG ABOUT WHERE TO LOOK. genetics_api_logs records NO SQL - its only log_type is endpoint_access and all 223k rows come from the file/tabix API, which never touches BigQuery. The only BigQuery SQL is in genetics_api_logs.stdout: 538 rows over 2026-05-21..2026-08-10, 375 referencing credible_sets_v. Small and agent/MCP-dominated - say so whenever these numbers are cited.

ACCEPTED COSTS, weighed against how often those columns are actually filtered: dataset= +267% at 3.5% of queries, gene_most_severe +44% at 6.1%, most_severe +8% at 4.8%, logical size +13.5%. The completely unfiltered scan gets 17% BETTER despite the bigger table, because both stored columns are cheaper to read than the columns needed to derive them (variant 1.96 GB stored vs 2.57 GB to derive; resource 1.25 GB vs 1.66 GB).

METHODOLOGY TRAP, recorded in the runbook: --dry_run CANNOT verify this. On a freshly-created table the estimate IGNORES clustering until BigQuery's storage optimiser has processed it - observed 4,492,232,401 B dry-run against 517,406,337 B actual. A first benchmark pass using dry-run showed the new tables as uniformly WORSE, entirely as an artefact. All recorded numbers are real total_bytes_processed with use_query_cache=False.

setup_bigquery.sh IS DANGEROUS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AND NEITHER PERFORMS THE SWAP. Without --recreate the DDL is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so editing a schema file and re-running prints 'Creating table credible_sets...', creates nothing and exits 0 - someone could believe they had swapped. With --recreate it bq rm's EVERY table in the dataset, not the one whose schema changed. It now prints what it is about to destroy with row counts and requires the dataset name typed. The guard is advisory - the row-count query fails open - and what is really wanted is a scoped --recreate <table>.

resource is GENERATED from datasets.yaml at load time rather than transcribed, so the mapping keeps one source of truth. Zero mismatches for both columns across all 115,043,095 benchmark rows. Declared NOT NULL, deviating from the CTAS-built experiment table, because api/main.py:499 reads a view column's mode from the base table and NULLABLE would flip /schema from REQUIRED for every MCP agent. No live row can violate it: the CASE ends ELSE LOWER(dataset) and chr/pos/ref/alt are all REQUIRED. View output schema verified byte-identical against the LIVE view: 22 columns, same names, order and types.

PERMANENT REGRESSION, documented in three places: resource is frozen at load time, so changing a dataset_to_resource_rules entry no longer takes effect by recreating the view - it needs a reload or an UPDATE backfill.

TWO REVIEW ROUNDS ON THE RUNBOOK, and the second earned its place. Round 1 found: the committed view SQL makes setup_bigquery.sh abort at credible_sets_v under pipefail, silently leaving the ELEVEN views sorting after it unapplied; the cutover left the view pointing at a renamed-away table for however long the operator takes to paste the next command, not 'a second'; a loader run during the soak DELETEs from the old table and then fails to re-append, destroying the rollback target; and the last-resort recovery used FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF, which does not work on a DROPPED table - it failed at exactly the moment it existed for.

THEN THE COLD RE-READ FOUND THIS BEAD'S OWN DEFECT CLASS IN ITS VERIFICATION SECTION: nothing asserted the new table actually HAS the target clustering. Since the DDL is IF NOT EXISTS, a leftover credible_sets_new from an aborted attempt would be reused with the wrong layout and pass every check - and the next section tells the reader that disappointing scan numbers are expected and to wait for the storage optimiser, which is precisely the explanation that would mask it. The layout is now asserted BEFORE cutover. Also fixed: no guard against running the 115M-row INSERT twice, an unguarded backfill UPDATE rewriting a clustering key table-wide with no preflight, a non-standard sed in one step that muscle memory would apply to the live table name, and a row count baked in as a literal in three places.

CROSS-REPO WORK STILL OWED, measured but NOT changed here: after the swap the note at configs/datasets.yaml:237 in the SUITE repo becomes WRONG. Re-measured with real execution: variant without chr goes 7,606,541,126 B to 253,707,488 B, and the chr-filter ratio goes from 0.048 (a 20.8x saving, so the note is exactly right today) to 1.136 (13.6% WORSE, so it becomes exactly wrong). Line 237's text and line 242's example SQL both need changing, and line ~1137 should switch to cs.variant = '5:1104823:C:T' instead of the four-column form. LEAVE ALONE the range-scan examples at 272, 304, 315, 1196, 1283 - they genuinely need chr = N for partition pruning - and 1033, 1052, 1082, which concern other tables. This must land in the same window as the swap.

NOT DONE, worth a bead if the swap proceeds: no test covers DERIVED_COLUMNS, resource_case_sql or the MATERIALIZED_RESOURCE_VIEWS lint branch. For a mechanism that bakes a value into 115M rows that is cheap insurance. Also noted: load_data.py and generate_resource_sql.py default to DIFFERENT datasets.yaml files (local generated copy vs canonical sibling); the rules blocks are identical today but drift is live, and a stale local copy would now silently mislabel an entire load.

TEST COUNT DISCREPANCY: the implementer reported 65 passing, the reviewer reproduced 49 - tests/test_build_phenotypes.py fails collection on missing fsspec, a pre-existing environment issue unrelated to this change. The reviewer asserted the worktree module path, so the 6o3 trap did not fire.

CLEANUP OWED: genetics-results-suite-4ci - drop credible_sets_exp_rdtp, credible_sets_exp_rdvp and credible_sets_exp_drvp. Keep drvp until the real swap is verified against it. Measurement cost was roughly 350-400 GB scanned, about USD 2-2.50.

title: Rewrite the system prompt for a code-first workflow
description:
defaults.py:185 currently says 'Prefer API tools over the database' and defaults.py:134 plus definitions.py:1477 mandate a get_database_schema call before any query. Under a code-first surface these are actively wrong - the mandated schema call is a guaranteed extra roundtrip, and the API-preference line inverts the intended routing.

Replace the per-tool routing guidance with code-first workflow guidance: how to discover capabilities, how to compose one script instead of several calls, when to print a summary rather than raw rows. Keep the substantive domain distinctions that are NOT about routing (the open_chromatin vs caQTL vs variant_effect vs mpra distinction at defaults.py:70-76 is real science and must survive, relocated into the SDK docs).

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/config/defaults.py.

title: Implement list_capabilities and read_artifact
description:
list_capabilities(module?) returns SDK stub signatures for one module, so the catalogue costs zero context until asked for. This is the mechanism that makes adding a dataset free in context terms.

read_artifact(path) pulls a file the script wrote (a plot, a TSV) out of the sandbox scratch dir. Reuse the existing path validation (_validate_path at genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/skills/sandbox_tools.py:26 — skills/, NOT tools/) - it exists because path traversal was already a concern in the in-process version.

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/tools/definitions.py, tools/executor.py.

NOTE 2026-08-13 (genetics-results-suite-5r2 batch): 5r2 claimed this bead 'names the wrong directory for sandbox_tools.py (tools/ instead of skills/)'. That claim was INACCURATE - the bead never spelled a directory for sandbox_tools.py at all; the 'tools/' in the Files line correctly refers to definitions.py and executor.py, which do live in tools/. The real defect was the missing path, which invited the misreading. Verified: skills/sandbox_tools.py has _ALLOWED_ENV_KEYS at line 21 and _validate_path at line 26.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-14 (tool halves only; the sandbox is not deployed).

genetics-mcp-server: tools/definitions.py (two TOOL_DEFINITIONS entries + register_mcp_tools blocks), tools/executor.py (list_capabilities, read_artifact, module-level SDK-catalogue renderers), mcp_server.py (_mcp_disabled), tests/test_code_execution_tools.py (new), tests/test_mcp_server.py. 1404 passed / 74 deselected (baseline 1372).

DECISIONS 4h6.16 SHOULD NOT RE-LITIGATE:
1. read_artifact IS in mcp_server._mcp_disabled already, added with the tool rather than in a later change; run_analysis still needs adding. list_capabilities is deliberately NOT excluded (renders SDK signatures from source; no data, no session state, no execution). tests/test_mcp_server.py pins both directions, and additionally asserts on the registered FastMCP tool list, not only the constant.
2. category = 'orchestration' for both (not 'general'): subagent.py drops the orchestration category, so a subagent cannot reach another execution's artifacts. NOTE for the 'code' profile: launch_subagents is also 'orchestration', so a category-only code profile would pull it in — the five-tool surface still needs name-level selection.
3. read_artifact reads the single dir named by SANDBOX_ARTIFACTS_DIR (unset everywhere today -> 'code execution is not enabled'), never SUBAGENT_ALLOWED_PATHS. Two-layer validation: bare-name check, then skills/sandbox_tools.py _validate_path on the resolved path (catches symlinks planted by the script). Out-of-allow-list reads answer 'not found' so probing discloses nothing. The HTTP proxy from chat-backend and the sid-scoped manifest resolution are 4h6.11's and are NOT implemented.

Docs: genetics-mcp-server/docs/project-spec.md gained a 'Code execution tools' section and its orchestration category row; genetics-results-suite docs/code-execution-security.md Layer 1 records what landed. While there, corrected that spec's orchestration row, which named a nonexistent 'run_subagents' — the tool is launch_subagents.
close_reason:
Landed as mcp ee313f2 + suite ab8c52d. FULL tier, and it needed all of it: implementation, sighted review + blind validator in parallel, TWO fix rounds, and a re-attack after each. mcp suite 1372 -> 1420 passed / 74 deselected. ruff clean. FILE-ONLY; the sandbox remains undeployed and nothing was turned on.

TWO WORKING PATH-TRAVERSAL ESCAPES WERE FOUND AND FIXED, both by RUNNING attacks rather than reading code, and both validators found them independently.
- TOCTOU: `_validate_path` resolved a path and returned a STRING, then the code re-opened it three more times (is_file, stat, read_bytes). A concurrent swapper leaked out-of-allow-list content 825 times in 6000 calls (13.75%) - not a narrow window, four separate lookups. It also threw an UNCAUGHT OSError out of the function 21/6000, carrying the absolute path, because the guard was `except ValueError` only.
- HARDLINK: `os.link(secret, artifacts/hard.db)` then reading it returned the content with success: True. A hardlink has nothing to resolve, so both path layers saw an in-tree path over an out-of-tree inode and passed. The threat model already assumed the script can plant a symlink in its own artifacts dir; the same privilege calls os.link.
- Also: pointing SANDBOX_ARTIFACTS_DIR at a SYMLINK defeated the allow-list entirely, because _validate_path resolves BOTH sides so they land on the same target. Reachable, not operator error: section 2 chowns /scratch/<id> to the child uid, so the child can rmdir its own artifacts and relink it at another execution's retained artifacts - the exact cross-execution channel 6.4 exists to prevent.

THE SECOND ROUND IS THE ONE WORTH REMEMBERING. Fixing the above with a single `os.open(..., O_NOFOLLOW)` was correct AND WAS THE SAME DEFECT ONE LEVEL UP: O_NOFOLLOW guards only the FINAL component, and `artifacts` is an INTERMEDIATE component the child owns. Swapping the directory between the check and the open leaked 151 times in 20000 (0.76%), and _validate_path was again no help because it resolves both sides through the same swapped link. THE REAL DEFECT WAS NEVER A MISSING FLAG - IT WAS ADDRESSING ANYTHING BY PATH AFTER CHECKING IT, and fixing that at one level only relocated it to the next.
FINAL SHAPE: `_open_artifacts_dir()` opens the directory once with O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW, verifies THAT DESCRIPTOR via /proc/self/fd (must sit under the hardcoded prefix, must not carry the kernel's " (deleted)" suffix), fails closed to None; the artifact is then opened as a BARE NAME with dir_fd=, and S_ISREG, st_nlink, the size gate and the chunked read all run against that one fd. Nothing is addressed by path afterwards.
RE-ATTACKED AT THE SAME SCALE: 0 leaks in 40000 iterations across two swapper profiles, and the deterministic control that previously returned the out-of-tree file now refuses. rmdir-then-recreate-at-the-same-path is refused by the " (deleted)" check, which is therefore load-bearing rather than hygiene. No descriptor leak over 5000 mixed refusals. With /proc/self/fd unreadable it fails CLOSED.

A TRIVIAL IN-SANDBOX DENIAL OF SERVICE WAS ALSO FOUND. `os.open` with O_RDONLY on a FIFO with no writer blocks IN THE KERNEL before S_ISREG is ever reached, so a script doing `os.mkfifo(artifacts/results.tsv)` hung the calling coroutine - and chat-backend with it - indefinitely. It hung the validator's own harness for ~4 minutes. O_NONBLOCK added; now refused in under a millisecond, and inert for regular files (a 3 MiB binary round-trips byte-identical, and the read loop drains on empty-chunk so a short read cannot truncate silently).

BOTH OF THE CHANGE'S ORIGINAL JUSTIFICATIONS WERE FALSE. That is the recurring failure mode in this epic and it recurred here twice in one task.
- "The `orchestration` category means a subagent can neither retrieve another execution's artifacts nor be told how to start one" - FALSE. subagent.py excludes orchestration BY NAME (`launch_subagents`), while TOOL_PROFILES puts orchestration in BOTH the api and bigquery profiles. Measured: both new tools were live in THREE OF FIVE subagent skills. Now excluded by name, INCLUDING the `skill.extra_tools` fallback path which re-derived tools from settings.disabled_tools and would have re-added them; a test loops every skill and fails under mutation.
- "list_capabilities discloses no data and an MCP client can already see what it renders" - FALSE. Diffed against all 67 MCP tool descriptions: it disclosed INTERNAL_API_SECRET's NAME, GENETICS_API_URL, BIGQUERY_API_URL, results-api, an internal bead id, _URL_SETTINGS, db-api, the quota numbers, and THAT A CODE-EXECUTION SANDBOX EXISTS - which is the thing the MCP exclusion set exists to keep off MCP. Module docstrings are now stripped, which removes the first five.
  MY OWN CORRECTION OF THIS WAS ALSO INCOMPLETE: I gave the fix agent a six-item residue list; re-derivation found FOUR MORE (the env-var mechanism sentence, the FinnGen LD server, the server-side execution model of limit=, and a fifth limit value MAX_ROWS=100000). The justification is therefore now stated BY CATEGORY - settings mechanism, internal service and component names, execution model, limit and quota values - with examples marked illustrative and the disclaimer that exhaustive enumeration was attempted twice and was incomplete both times. That is the durable shape; do not replace it with a third list.

MCP EXCLUSION DECISIONS, both deliberate and both pinned by tests: read_artifact IS excluded, in the same change that defines it, because a tool is registered on /mcp the moment its definition exists unless excluded - deferring to 4h6.16 would have shipped a live window. list_capabilities is deliberately NOT excluded: padding the set with names that are not security controls stops the next reader being able to tell which entries are load-bearing. Verified by running: 54 registered, read_artifact absent, and the pin fails under in-memory mutation.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE SPEC, accepted: docs/code-execution-security.md specifies that read_artifact proxies over HTTP and never reads the local filesystem in chat-backend. There is no sandbox HTTP service to proxy to yet, so this implements the filesystem side and leaves the proxy client and sid-scoped manifest resolution to 4h6.11. The gate was made SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by configuration discipline: the artifacts dir must resolve under a hardcoded /scratch/ prefix, and chat-backend has no such volume and never will, so SANDBOX_ARTIFACTS_DIR=/data - the PVC holding chat_history.db and llm_config.db - cannot resolve. Before the prefix, a single unset env var was the entire safety property.

STATED LIMITATIONS, recorded in the security doc rather than left implicit: the prefix check is a LOCATION check and not an OWNERSHIP one, so a directory that merely sits under the prefix is readable (not reachable from a script - it needs the parent's environment). CROSS-EXECUTION SCOPING IS NOT IMPLEMENTED: there is no session or execution parameter, so which execution's artifacts are reachable rests entirely on the env var, constrained only by the structural checks. And an availability note: a masked or restricted /proc makes the descriptor verification fail closed and refuse EVERYTHING - worth confirming once when 4h6.7 writes the Deployment.

NOT FIXED, deliberately: the symlink-refused path returns ~35% faster than other refusals because _validate_path raises before the open. It reveals only whether a name the caller planted is an out-of-tree symlink, and a dangling symlink takes the same fast path, so it is not an existence oracle. Noted in the justification.

CORRECTION TO THE IMPLEMENTATION REPORT: it claimed to have fixed a docs/project-spec.md row naming a nonexistent `run_subagents`. `git show HEAD` shows that row already read `launch_subagents`; there was nothing to fix, and the three surviving `run_subagents()` references are the real SubagentService method, correctly untouched.

FOLLOW-UP OWNED ELSEWHERE: 4h6.16 still owns run_analysis, the `code` TOOL_PROFILE and the route-level assertion. Note for whoever takes it - a category-only `code` profile would pull in launch_subagents, since it is also `orchestration`; the five-tool surface needs name-level selection.

title: Generate schema markdown and .pyi stubs into the sandbox image at build time
description:
This is how the agent learns the schema without any of it being front-loaded into context - the progressive-disclosure half of Alt 3, and the reason it needs no prompt-cache breakpoint (genetics-mcp-server/docs/project-spec.md:420 records that there is no spare breakpoint).

Generate from the canonical configs/datasets.yaml at image build: /genetics/schema/<view>.md (one file per view, columns + descriptions + the worked examples already in the tables.<view>.examples blocks) and /genetics/sdk/*.pyi signature stubs. A script reads them on demand like a developer would.

Include the hard-won correctness rules as prose in the relevant schema files: the peak_to_gene join warning (datasets.yaml:204-210), the chr-alongside-variant partition-pruning rule (datasets.yaml:237), and the credible-set key being (resource, dataset, trait, cell_type, cs_id) not cs_id alone.

Files: genetics-results-db or genetics-mcp-server build script (new), sandbox Dockerfile.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 3e4425f and genetics-mcp-server efc77a2. Files only; NOTHING applied to any cluster, no docker push. Validation: mechanics review + CONTENT validation in parallel, two fix rounds, a targeted re-review, then a final correction round. No blocking findings survived.

THIS UNBLOCKS A REAL IMAGE BUILD. 4h6.6 deliberately made the build REFUSE while PLACEHOLDER files were staged, so this is the first point where the sandbox image actually builds: docker build succeeds locally with all ten of that bead's assertions passing, and NO Dockerfile change was needed - the 4h6.6 contract held exactly as written (sandbox/schema -> /genetics/schema, sandbox/stubs -> /genetics/sdk, verbatim, 65532:65532, /genetics/sdk NOT on PYTHONPATH).

WHAT LANDED. scripts/gen-sandbox-docs.py renders 15 view files plus an index into sandbox/schema/ and three .pyi stubs into sandbox/stubs/, from canonical configs/datasets.yaml and the SDK source. scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py is a 13-check harness now gating build.sh. SUITE has no pytest suite; the convention is standalone scripts/test-*.py with a check() decorator and exit 0/1/2, which this follows.

GENERATED, NEVER TRANSCRIBED, AND ENFORCED. The generator names no view and no SDK function in its executable code; the harness proves it by AST-stripping the generator's own comments and docstrings and asserting on what remains. That constraint is load-bearing: 5p5 will rewrite the variant/chr guidance the moment the credible_sets clustering swap runs, and a transcribed rule would then be silently wrong inside the image while datasets.yaml said the opposite. Views come from yaml.safe_load, not a regex - 15, cross-checked against db-api's own VIEWS. Stubs are read with ast, never imported, since importing would execute config.settings and the build host has no polars or httpx.

DELIBERATE EDIT TO THE CANONICAL configs/datasets.yaml. The credible-set key was the one rule not expressible from any existing field - columns.cs_id said only 'groups variants in the same causal signal'. Written into that description rather than hardcoded in the generator. Verified against live BigQuery, not asserted: chr22 alone has 41,412 distinct cs_id against 122,322 distinct 5-tuples, a 3x silent merge; trait is load-bearing (dropping it gives 120,761); the key does not over-merge because cs_id is itself region-qualified. Doc-ownership judged and confirmed: datasets-yaml-schema.md documents columns.<name> as free-text, no enum/field/view list changed, so no doc was made stale. No sibling repo TRACKS a datasets.yaml copy - all are gitignored - and all four generated copies were synced by hand because scripts/sync-datasets.sh is worktree-unaware and exits 0 having copied nothing.

TWO DEFECTS THAT WOULD HAVE SHIPPED WRONG ANSWERS, both found by validating CONTENT rather than code - asking whether an LLM reading these files would write correct SQL. Neither was visible to the mechanics review.

1. coloc_credsets_v documented a join key that is NOT a key. On (dataset, cs_id), UKB_PPP's chr22:42428847-45428847_1 spans 71 distinct traits, because for GWAS and pQTL cs_id encodes the fine-mapping REGION, not the trait. The doc's own worked example returned the right answer BY LUCK - the top hit landed in a region no other FinnGen_R14 trait occupies. In a dense region it silently mixed dozens of unrelated proteins' PIPs into the answer. It also contradicted credible_sets_v.md, which had it right.
   THE OBVIOUS REPAIR WAS ALSO WRONG and only measuring caught it: joining on trait works for GWAS and DESTROYS the QTL side, because colocalization_v.trait2 is a gene symbol where coloc_credsets_v.trait is the molecular feature id - zero rows for 3,574 of 3,785 eQTL sides and 469 of 473 sQTL. Shipped join uses trait_original with cell_type IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, verified across all five verticals: GWAS 1174/1174 with the NULL-safe form vs 0/1174 with plain equality, caQTL 3723/3723, pQTL 258/258, eQTL 4442/4466, sQTL 469/473.
2. All 54 worked examples used unqualified view names. NOT a live 400 on the sql() path - db-api's _qualify_tables rewrites them before authorize_query - but that fallback is a regex whose own docstring records it cannot see inside string literals, and an agent copying an example anywhere else gets 'must be qualified with a dataset'. 69 references qualified at the source, zero double-qualifications, CTE names and aliases untouched, all 52 examples dry-run clean.

THREE THINGS WRITTEN DOWN BACKWARDS AND CAUGHT BY RE-MEASURING - worth noting because each was produced by a careful agent and refuted by data:
- The residual unmatched sides are FinnLiver, DATASET-WIDE (24/24 eQTL, 4/4 sQTL), not an eQTL Catalogue tail - that resource contributes zero - and the suffix is on coloc_credsets_v, not colocalization_v. An earlier round asserted a SPLIT fallback does not recover them; it recovers all 28 with zero ambiguity, but ONLY if both sides are split (splitting one side gives 947/4466 and breaks the 3.5k pairs that already matched).
- The example demonstrating the bad join was pinned by ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 over 47 rows tied at PP_H4_abf = 1.0, so its numbers were irreproducible and both joins returned identically. With a deterministic tiebreak: 2 credible sets against 18 under the shortened join.
- coloc_credsets_v repeats a variant on 4,443 of 20,050 keys (22%, against credible_sets_v's 2.4%), so its variant-intersection example double-counted. Now documented with the SELECT DISTINCT remedy.

The cs_id wording ALSO had to name IS NOT DISTINCT FROM explicitly: cell_type is NULL for GWAS on 282,195 of 2,489,585 chr22 rows, so a plain equi-join on the five columns silently drops every GWAS row. The first version said 'grouping, joining or counting' without qualification, which is right for GROUP BY and wrong for JOIN.

HARNESS HARDENING after mutation testing found two ways to pass on bad output: _stub_surface was NAMED 'exactly the SDK's exported surface' and cited 4h6.6's equality precedent while asserting CONTAINMENT, so a FABRICATED function in genetics.pyi passed all 13 checks - the model would have been shown an SDK function that does not exist. And categorical_columns had NO coverage, so dropping the whole block regenerated cleanly. Both closed. The harness was also wired to nothing; it now gates build.sh (hard fail) and folds into build-all.sh's skip branch, and returns exit 2 rather than 0 when the SDK source is absent instead of silently running 9 of 13.

MAX_ROWS is DERIVED by following client.py into ToolExecutor._MAX_SQL_LIMIT and SystemExits if unresolvable. 6uk's empty-result warning moved from hla()'s docstring alone to the SDK module docstring covering all nine results-api-backed functions. sql() raises rather than returning a prefix at its ceiling; now stated.

VERIFIED: 13/13 harness checks, with the two new ones confirmed to FAIL on their mutations; all 52 examples dry-run clean; docker build 10 assertions ok / 0 failures; column lists exact for all 15 views against INFORMATION_SCHEMA (same columns, count and order, zero undocumented, zero nonexistent, no post-swap credible_sets shape leaked); stub fidelity exact by AST diff of all 26 GeneticsClient methods; MCP 1285 passed / 74 deselected, unchanged.

LEFT UNDONE, filed: 4h6.30 (per-view partitioning/clustering docs - deliberately NOT written, because 4h6.18 is about to change credible_sets's clustering and anything written today goes stale on swap; deps added on 4h6.18 and 5p5), 4h6.31 (column TYPE field - a datasets.yaml schema change requiring datasets-yaml-schema.md and adding-datasets.md updates; an agent currently cannot know cs_id is STRING, that chr is INT64 so chr = 'chr5' fails, or that gene_group_ids is an ARRAY needing UNNEST), 4h6.32 (SDK truncation message names 100,000 when a sandbox execution is capped at 25,000), fml (adding-datasets.md says two views are excluded from ALL_VIEWS; there are four).

NOTE FOR ANYONE RUNNING THE SCRIPTS BY HAND: both refuse to run from a worktree without --sdk-src, since they look for sandbox/.sdk-src. A bare invocation reports 'harness cannot run' (exit 2) rather than passing. Pre-existing to this bead's wiring, not a regression.

title: Instrument every SDK function call so the audit trail survives
description:
Today each data access is a tool call, logged as 'Executing tool: <name>' (llm_service.py:869) and countable per conversation. Once access moves inside a script, that trail disappears and analyze_conversations' per-tool statistics lose their meaning.

Emit a structured log line per SDK function call from inside the sandbox, carrying session id, function name, arguments summary and row count, mirroring the existing format so existing log queries keep working. This is both an observability requirement and a security requirement (the security doc needs to answer 'what did that script actually read?').

Files: genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/sdk/ (instrumentation decorator), scripts/analyze_conversations.py (consume SDK-function stats alongside tool stats).
close_reason:
Landed as mcp bdeda40 + suite e4726fb. FULL tier - implementation, blind validator, TWO fix rounds with a re-attack after each. mcp suite 1420 -> 1487 passed / 74 deselected. ruff clean. list_capabilities output verified BYTE-IDENTICAL against HEAD (sha256 equal) because 4h6.15 ships tests over it.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS FALSE and the implementation caught it. The bead says each access is "logged as `Executing tool:` and countable per conversation", treating those as one record. THEY NEVER WERE: analyze_conversations.py reads NO LOGS AT ALL - it counts tool calls from chat_messages.content_json tool_use blocks with a display-marker fallback. So the log line and the analyzer's input were always different things. This mirrors the LOG format (where an operator's queries live) and gives the analyzer a NEW log-file input, because SDK calls happen in another process and are never persisted as message content. The report distinguishes "no --sdk-log supplied" from "empty log" rather than printing a misleading zero.
