title: Phase 0: finalize EpiMap 18-state storage + open/active state set
description: Decide how the ChromHMM 18-state label is stored (score_type=chromhmm_18state + state token placement) and which states count as open/active (TSS/enhancer/transcribed). Gates the EpiMap munge task.
design:
EpiMap ChromHMM 18-state modeling for the open_chromatin product.
Model = Roadmap/EpiMap 18-state (observed_aux_18), 833 biosamples, hg38 CALLS.
INCLUDE (accessible/active regulatory subset) as open_chromatin rows:
  active promoter: TssA, TssFlnk, TssFlnkU, TssFlnkD
  active enhancer: EnhA1, EnhA2, EnhG1, EnhG2, EnhWk
  poised/bivalent (accessible, tagged): TssBiv, EnhBiv
EXCLUDE (not open peaks): Tx, TxWk, ZNF_Rpts, Het, ReprPC, ReprPCWk, Quies.
State storage (NO schema change): encode the exact state in score_type as chromhmm:<State> (e.g. score_type=chromhmm:EnhA1); assay=chromHMM; score=NULL (presence-based — ChromHMM is a categorical segmentation, so row existence = state called in that biosample).
Agent-facing regulatory_class grouping (map in the MCP tool description, NOT stored): Tss* -> promoter, Enh* -> enhancer, *Biv -> bivalent.
Labels: cell_type = verbatim EpiMap biosample name; tissue from EpiMap sample metadata (GROUP/Anatomy column); life_stage=adult unless the biosample metadata marks it fetal/embryonic; condition=unknown.
Do NOT import EpiMap DNase layer (that is the Meuleman DHS index, which was dropped).
close_reason: Resolved: EpiMap active/accessible state subset + state-in-score_type encoding decided. Decision recorded in --design.

title: Phase 0: confirm genome builds & liftOver needs
description: Confirm all sources vs hg38: Marderstein/Li/Catlas/ROSMAP snATAC and EpiMap ChromHMM CALLS are hg38; Calderon is hg19 (needs liftOver). Verify EpiMap hg38 CALLS are used, not hg19. Gates all munge tasks.
design:
Genome-build decision — platform standard = GRCh38/hg38 (GENCODE).
- marderstein (scATAC peaks + ChromBPNet + FLARE): hg38, native, no liftOver.
- li_brain_atac (Li 2023 Science): hg38, native.
- catlas (Zhang 2021 Cell): hg38, native (verify cCRE BED header at download).
- epimap (Boix 2021): USE the hg38 CALLS directory (ChromHMM observed_aux_18_hg38), NOT hg19.
- calderon_immune (Calderon 2019): hg19 -> liftOver to hg38 (UCSC hg19ToHg38.over.chain); drop unmapped and split/multi-mapping intervals, then re-sort.
- rosmap_brain (Xiong 2023): hg38, native.
RULE for every munge task: verify the source file build at download; if hg19, liftOver to hg38 and drop unmapped/multimapped before bgzip+tabix. Only Calderon is known-hg19 today.
close_reason: Resolved: builds determined (all hg38 except Calderon hg19->liftOver; EpiMap use hg38 CALLS). Per-file verification folded into each munge task. Decision recorded in --design.

title: Feature: Google token authentication for MCP server
description:
Currently the MCP server (genetics-mcp-server/src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py) only accepts MCP_API_KEY shared secrets and user-created API tokens (validated via local DB or chat-backend /v1/tokens/validate). It does NOT support Google Identity Tokens.

The results-api (genetics-results-api/app/core/auth.py) already supports all three methods: internal secret, user tokens, and Google Identity Tokens (JWT validated via google.oauth2.id_token.verify_oauth2_token with email_verified + allowed domain checks).

Goal: Bring MCP server bearer token auth to parity with results-api by adding Google Identity Token validation. This enables programmatic clients to authenticate to /mcp using gcloud-issued ID tokens, just like they already can with /api.
close_reason: All 6 subtasks complete: google-auth dep added (.1), settings fields added (.2), JWT validation branch implemented (.3), unit tests added (.4), shared bearer-auth-allowed ConfigMap created and wired into both mcp-server and results-api (.5), documentation updated (.6). MCP server now has bearer-token auth parity with results-api.

title: rollout.sh has no `sandbox` entry, so build.sh prints a command that fails
description:
FOUND during genetics-results-suite-4h6.7's review, by BOTH validators independently. Pre-existing (the sandbox image build landed in 4h6.6), but 4h6.7 is what makes a single-service sandbox rollout meaningful, so it is worth fixing now rather than when someone first needs it in a hurry.

THE DEFECT: `scripts/build.sh:91` prints, as the next step after building the sandbox image,
    To roll out: REGISTRY=... ./scripts/rollout.sh sandbox ${TAG}
`scripts/rollout.sh`'s IMAGE_MAP (~lines 40-48) has NO `sandbox` key, so that exact command exits 1 with `Unknown service: sandbox`. The tool tells you to run something that cannot work.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: this makes the sandbox THE ONLY WORKLOAD WITH NO SINGLE-SERVICE UPDATE PATH. Every other service can be rolled individually; the sandbox can only be updated by a full `scripts/deploy.sh`, which also runs `terraform apply -auto-approve` and restarts everything else. That is a bad property for the one workload most likely to need a quick targeted redeploy, and neither README.md nor docs/project-spec.md says so.

THE FIX IS ONE LINE: add `[sandbox]=sandbox` to IMAGE_MAP. Both validators checked the shape - the image repo and the container name are both literally `sandbox`, so CONTAINER_NAME resolves correctly with no special-casing.

CHECK BEFORE COMMITTING, because the sandbox is not an ordinary service:
- rollout.sh restarts a Deployment. The sandbox Deployment is `strategy: Recreate` with `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 130`, so a rollout KILLS AN IN-FLIGHT EXECUTION and leaves no sandbox for up to ~130s. Confirm the script's rollout-status wait tolerates that, and that its timeout exceeds the grace period.
- The sandbox Deployment is GATED: `deploy.sh` only applies it when ENABLE_SANDBOX is on, derived from `sandbox_pool_enabled = true` in terraform.tfvars. Decide what `rollout.sh sandbox` should do when no sandbox Deployment exists in the cluster - a clear "not deployed" message beats a kubectl error.
- The doc-ownership table makes `scripts/*.sh` changes require updating docs/project-spec.md and README.md in the same commit.

NOT URGENT: the sandbox is not deployed, and nothing can be rolled out until 4h6.14 provides a supervisor for the image to run.

title: The sandbox startup gate accepts a blank-ish signing key - add a length check, but do NOT strip
description:
FOUND while validating genetics-results-suite-l7z and deliberately NOT fixed there - it is PRE-EXISTING (the pre-l7z import-time snapshot used the identical truthiness test), orthogonal to that task's claim, and the obvious one-line fix is WRONG in a way worth recording.

THE GAP: `require_sandbox_config` accepts any truthy string as SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY. Measured with SANDBOX_ENABLED=true, all of these pass startup: "   ", "\n", "x", "0". PyJWT itself warns - `InsecureKeyLengthWarning: The HMAC key is 3 bytes long`.
CONSEQUENCE: a whitespace-only or single-character secret - the classic `kubectl create secret --from-file` of an empty or near-empty file - passes the startup gate AND becomes a guessable HMAC key that mints valid sandbox principals. The startup check exists precisely to stop the sandbox reaching a misconfigured db-api, and this is a misconfiguration it does not catch.

THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG. Do NOT just add .strip() to `_signing_key()`. db-api VERIFIES with that value; chat-backend MINTS with whatever is in its own copy of the secret. A key deployed with a trailing newline signs as "key\n" and would then be verified against "key", so EVERY LEGITIMATE SANDBOX TOKEN WOULD 401. Any normalisation has to happen on both sides at once, which means a coordinated change in the minting repo - that is why l7z declined it rather than doing it cheaply.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK, roughly in order of cost:
1. A MINIMUM-LENGTH GATE AT STARTUP ONLY, with no normalisation - e.g. refuse to start if the key is shorter than N bytes after stripping, WITHOUT changing the value used for signing or verifying. This catches the whole reported class ("   ", "\n", "x", "0") and cannot desynchronise anything, because the value that reaches jwt.decode is untouched. This is almost certainly the right answer, and it is self-contained.
2. Additionally warn (not fail) if the key differs from its stripped form, so a trailing-newline secret is VISIBLE rather than silently load-bearing.
3. Only if 1 and 2 are judged insufficient: coordinated normalisation across the minter and verifier, which needs both repos changed and deployed together and is the risky option.

WHERE: `api/sandbox_auth.py`'s `require_sandbox_config` in genetics-results-db. Note it runs at IMPORT and its remedy is sys.exit(1), which is correct there - the pod never passes readiness and the rollout stalls, so a bad key is caught before the pod serves.

NOT URGENT: the sandbox is not deployed (SANDBOX_ENABLED is "false" on both services and there is no k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml), so no such key exists yet. Do it before the sandbox ships, since after that a weak key is a live credential rather than a configuration hazard.

title: Document (or close by observation) the BigQuery remote-function egress residual in the SQL gate
description:
FOUND while validating genetics-results-suite-4h6.33's claim that db-api is a safe permitted egress target for the sandbox. It IS safe against every path that was checked - this is the one residual that was not, and it is not documented anywhere.

WHAT WAS VERIFIED AND HOLDS: db-api is a permitted egress target that executes SQL, and authorize_query (genetics-results-db api/main.py:370-414) dry-runs each statement through BigQuery and rejects statement_type != "SELECT" plus any table outside _ALLOWED_TABLE_IDS. That closes EXPORT DATA, EXECUTE IMMEDIATE, DDL and DML as outbound data paths.

THE RESIDUAL: a BigQuery REMOTE FUNCTION (or a remote-model/`ML.PREDICT`-style construct) invoked inside an otherwise-legitimate SELECT would pass BOTH gates - the statement really is a SELECT, and ROUTINES DO NOT APPEAR IN referenced_tables, which is what the allow-list is checked against. A remote function calls a Cloud Run/Cloud Functions endpoint with the row values, so it is an egress channel that neither the NetworkPolicy nor the SQL gate sees, because the call is made BY BIGQUERY, not by the sandbox pod.

WHY THIS IS LOW SEVERITY TODAY, and file it as hardening rather than a hole: creating a remote function requires CREATE FUNCTION, which is DDL, which the same statement_type gate blocks. So it only matters if a remote function ALREADY EXISTS in the project, or if something outside this path can create one. It also requires a BigQuery Connection, which is an IAM-governed resource.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY DO, cheapest first:
1. ESTABLISH THE FACT: enumerate existing routines and connections in the project and record the answer. If there are none, say so in docs/code-execution-security.md and the residual is closed by observation. Read-only: `bq ls --routines` per dataset, and list BigQuery connections.
2. If any exist, decide whether the dry-run gate should additionally reject statements whose referenced routines are not allow-listed - note dry-run metadata may or may not expose routines, so CHECK WHETHER IT IS EVEN DETECTABLE before designing on it.
3. Confirm no service account reachable from this path holds bigquery.connections.use or the ability to create routines in the datasets involved.

WHERE IT BELONGS: docs/code-execution-security.md owns the egress and SQL-gate analysis. Its section 3 currently reasons entirely about POD egress; a remote function is egress that does not originate in the pod, which is the reason it is not covered by anything written there.

NOTE THE SANDBOX IS NOT DEPLOYED, so this is design-time - the cheapest point to settle it.

title: api/sandbox_auth.py still snapshots two auth env vars at import - the hazard xi6 fixed for the third
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-xi6, which fixed this hazard for ONE of the three auth-related env vars and deliberately left the other two. Both the sighted reviewer and the blind validator raised it independently.

api/sandbox_auth.py:58 and :63 still snapshot SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY and SANDBOX_ENABLED AT IMPORT - exactly the pattern xi6 removed for INTERNAL_API_SECRET. So "whoever imports first decides" still holds for the sandbox credential path, which is the one path with ATTACKER-AUTHORED input.

CONCRETE CONSEQUENCES ESTABLISHED DURING xi6:
- tests/conftest.py's restore_auth_env fixture restores all three variables as if they were symmetric. Restoring the two sandbox ones buys NOTHING behavioural: they cannot change an already-imported module, so only a _reload() (which pops and re-imports them itself) ever sees them. The fixture's own docstring was corrected to say so, but the asymmetry remains in the code.
- A test that pops SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY affects no live app object, and popping it would fail CLOSED rather than open - so this is a correctness-and-clarity problem, not a security hole today.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING ANYWAY: the sandbox path is the one an attacker-authored script reaches. Leaving it on the pattern that just produced a seed-dependent red suite in the shared-secret path means the next person to add a module-scope import gets the same class of failure, in the harder-to-reason-about credential.

DO NOT COPY xi6's SOLUTION BLINDLY. xi6 needed a one-way latch and a tri-state return because its variable governs a FAIL-OPEN branch; the sandbox path has no fail-open equivalent (an unset signing key rejects every token), so a plain per-request read may well be sufficient. Establish that before designing.
Check also whether require_sandbox_config's invariant ("sandbox deployed => internal secret present") should be re-checked per request rather than only at import - xi6 left it asserted at startup only, which is recorded there as a known limitation.
close_reason:
Landed as genetics-results-db e7881bf. Blind validator + one fix round. db suite 148 -> 154 passed on the worktree's own .venv, stable at seeds 2662673150 (the historically red one), 12345 and 987654321. FILE-ONLY.
TIER NOTE, stated so the record is accurate: I ran the BLIND validator but NOT a sighted review alongside it. The blind pass was thorough and found everything below, but this was Standard-plus rather than the Full tier an auth path nominally calls for.

THE DESIGN CALL WAS "NO LATCH", AND IT SURVIVED DIRECT ATTACK. The bead warned against copying xi6 blindly and that warning paid: xi6 needed a one-way latch and a tri-state return because its value governs a FAIL-OPEN branch - "" means "authentication was never configured" and require_auth answers it with an early return that ADMITS the caller, so a plain read could DISABLE authentication in a running process. The signing key has no value with that meaning. verify_sandbox_token raises on an empty key and require_auth converts SandboxTokenError into a hard 401 with no fallthrough, so every state except the exact minting key rejects, and the only runtime transitions a plain read admits are unset->set (the hazard being removed) and set->unset-or-changed, both strictly STRICTER. A latch would have been a process global a future reader must trace before discovering it can never change an outcome.
MEASURED, not argued: unset / empty / trailing-newline / rotated / wrong-key tokens all 401; a non-ASCII but valid-UTF-8 key that MATCHES correctly returns 200 (key equality, no ASCII invariant needed here unlike the shared secret); an unset INTERNAL_API_SECRET - which IS fail-open - plus an INVALID sandbox token still 401, proving the sandbox path does not inherit the early return; and with two Authorization headers Starlette returns the first, so header stuffing can neither downgrade a failed sandbox token onto the secret path nor upgrade anything without already knowing the secret.

ONE FINDING WITH RUNTIME CONSEQUENCE, fixed. The catch was `except jwt.InvalidTokenError`. jwt.InvalidKeyError is a SIBLING under PyJWTError, NOT a subclass - a PEM pasted into the env var raises it - and PyJWT's prepare_key encodes a str key as UTF-8, so a key carrying the surrogates os.environ produces from non-UTF-8 bytes raises UnicodeEncodeError. Both escaped uncaught and surfaced as 500 RATHER THAN 401. Still fail-closed - nobody was admitted - but it falsified the function's own "always a hard 401" docstring and SUPPRESSED THE endpoint_access REJECTION LOG, so an operator saw an unattributed 500 instead of an auth failure. This is also the one place xi6's latin-1/utf-8 concern genuinely recurs, and the module had not addressed it.
Widened to `except Exception`, deliberately over the narrower tuple: the try block wraps exactly ONE call (jwt.decode), so the breadth cannot swallow surrounding logic, and only the broad form makes the "raises only SandboxTokenError" contract literally true against a future crypto-layer raise type. Justified in a comment. Two new parametrized tests pin it - one through the app asserting 401-not-500 and that the shared-secret caller is unaffected, one asserting the exception type directly. Nothing in the suite had pinned this before.

require_sandbox_config STAYS STARTUP-ONLY, and the question xi6 left open is now closed rather than deferred a third time. Reasons written into the docstring: its remedy is sys.exit(1), which is only correct at import (the pod never passes readiness, the rollout stalls, old pods keep serving) whereas from a request path it would kill a serving pod at a moment THE SANDBOX - the one attacker-authored caller - chooses; and SANDBOX_ENABLED comes from the pod spec, which cannot change without a new pod that re-runs the check.
MY FIRST DRAFT OF THAT ARGUMENT WAS WRONG AND THE VALIDATOR BUILT THE COUNTEREXAMPLE. It asserted "there is no runtime state this check could catch in which the service is serving fail-open with the sandbox deployed". That covers only the emptied-AFTER-startup transitions and omits the NEVER-CONFIGURED case, where _authentication_was_configured is False and _internal_api_secret() returns "" rather than None. Starting a process with both variables unset (so the check returns early) and then flipping SANDBOX_ENABLED=true reaches exactly that state. The CONCLUSION stands - pod-environment immutability rescues it - so the wording now depends on that rather than asserting the state cannot exist. Same edit in db docs/project-spec.md.

TESTS: the four simplified tests were checked for whether they still bite, and the honest answer is that only ONE of them does (the three-param startup test). The regression pressure comes from the two NEW tests, both of which fail against a reintroduced import-time snapshot. One simplified test - test_signing_key_unset_rejects_every_sandbox_token - was passing WITHOUT its delenv having any effect, since under a frozen empty key the sandbox path is already dead; it now asserts a non-401 BEFORE the delenv so it proves the path was live and the unset killed it.
The implementation reported "6 failed / 33 passed" when it verified the tests bite; independent re-measurement got 7/32 key-only and 9/30 for both variables. The conclusion is unaffected. Grepped tests/, docs/ and api/ - the figure was never written into a file, so there is nothing to correct.

WHAT THE BEAD GOT WRONG, two refinements: it framed SANDBOX_ENABLED as symmetric with the signing key, but only the signing key is on a request path at all - SANDBOX_ENABLED is read solely by the startup check, so moving it off the snapshot buys correctness of the CHECK, not any request-time behaviour. And it treated require_sandbox_config's scope as an open question inherited from xi6; it is closed by xi6's landed latch plus this change together, which is a conclusion xi6 could not have drawn before its own latch existed.

DECLINED, with a better reason than my instruction had, and filed separately: I asked for .strip() on the signing key so the startup gate would reject a whitespace-only secret. The fix agent refused correctly - stripping on the VERIFY side desynchronizes db-api from chat-backend's MINTING side, so a key deployed via `kubectl create secret --from-file` with a trailing newline signs as "key\n" and would then verify against "key", 401ing every legitimate sandbox token. That needs a coordinated change in the minting repo.

CONFIRMED CLEAN, so nobody re-derives it: no other module-scope auth-relevant env snapshot remains in api/ (only _startup_secret, by design, and CORS_ORIGINS whose middleware is constructed at import so a per-call read would be meaningless); no lru_cache/cache/cached_property anywhere in api/; FastAPI does not cache a plain function dependency across requests; and the per-call read costs 697ns against a 69.3us HMAC verify, i.e. 1%.

title: Raw resource reaches logger.error in three executor.py sites - establish whether the sink makes it log injection
description:
Found by a probe during the fml/5r2/7zr/bi1/dqa batch and deliberately left out of it - unrelated to that change, and a different property from the one that batch fixed.

genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/tools/executor.py: raw `resource` reaches logger.error f-strings at roughly lines 1022, 1847 and 1881. RE-LOCATE WITH grep RATHER THAN TRUSTING THESE LINE NUMBERS - this file's numbering has already shifted once mid-investigation and a bead in this backlog was filed on stale coordinates.

These are results-api-facing functions where `resource` is never SQL-quoted or normalized at all, so this is NOT the quote_literal asymmetry that batch closed (that one is complete: both quote_literal(resource) sites now normalize). The question here is narrower and worth answering rather than assuming: a caller-supplied value containing CR/LF reaching a log line is log injection if the sink is line-oriented. The suite ships a structured logging path and a BigQuery endpoint_access sink, so it may well be a non-issue - CHECK WHICH SINK THESE ERRORS LAND IN before doing anything. If the sink is structured, close this as not-a-defect and record why, so it is not rediscovered.

VERIFY THE PREMISE FIRST. It rests on a single probe's grep and has not been independently confirmed.

title: Batched nits from the doc-accuracy pass: exclusions that are true only by accident
description:
Batched nits from the fml/5r2/7zr/bi1/dqa doc-accuracy pass (suite 1b1d37b, mcp ae805df). All established by running commands, not by reading. None is a defect today; each is a justification or an exclusion that is true only by accident.

Changing parent= swaps the entire login page including which authenticator forms render. Same list exempts .svg, which can embed <script>. Narrow to the asset types that genuinely cannot carry logic, or exempt by directory-plus-extension.
2. Same regex is CASE-SENSITIVE, so logo.PNG warns. Over-fires only; harmless.
3. Same file, the justification comment says branding assets "change how the login page looks and reads and has no other effect". 5. scripts/check-doc-drift.sh, PRE-EXISTING and out of scope for that pass: the k8s, terraform and ops-scripts rows name the doc pair project-spec.md + README.md, but DOCS_SPEC is an ALTERNATION, so touching either doc alone satisfies the rule and silences it. The row promises both are checked; the rule checks either.
6. Staging k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml emits two separate warnings both pointing at docs/project-spec.md (the ^k8s/ rule and the sandbox project-spec rule). Duplicate noise of the same family dqa complained about, though not a false positive. Pre-existing.

APPENDED FROM genetics-results-suite-xi6 (db 515851c), same batching rule - neither is a defect today:

Because conftest's restore_auth_env is function-scoped it snapshots AFTER that fixture ran, so it preserves the value rather than clearing it - measured: after `pytest tests/test_api_auth.py` the session ends with INTERNAL_API_SECRET='test-internal-secret' PROJECT_ID='test-project' still set. title: Decide auth-gateway's image refresh policy - the tag is effectively frozen today
description:
Filed from genetics-results-suite-o5i, which chose NOT to pin auth-gateway's image digest and recorded the tested digest in a comment instead. Review accepted that as a decision rather than an evasion, but pointed out the stated benefit is not actually being realised.

THE POSITION TODAY, all verified: k8s/deployments/auth-gateway.yaml uses `nginx:1.27-alpine` with NO imagePullPolicy, so it defaults to IfNotPresent. `grep -rn "image:" k8s/` finds 15 references and ZERO digests, so tag-only is genuinely the repo convention. There is no .github, no Renovate, no Dependabot, no cloudbuild and no gitlab-ci anywhere in the tree - NOTHING would ever bump a pin. That was the argument against pinning: it would freeze an internet-facing HTTP parser permanently.
The digest the tag resolves to today, sha256:65645c7bb6a0661892a8b03b89d0743208a18dd2f3f17a54ef4b76fb8e2f2a10, was created 2025-04-16 and is EXACTLY what the live pod is running.

REVIEW'S COUNTERPOINT, which is the reason this bead exists: with IfNotPresent on a SINGLE-NODE cluster, the image is already effectively frozen at that Apr-2025 digest until the node is replaced. So not pinning does not buy CVE pickup - it only makes the freeze implicit instead of explicit, and dependent on node lifecycle rather than on a decision. The honest resolutions are:
  (a) imagePullPolicy: Always - makes the not-pinning argument true, at the cost of a pull on every pod start and a gateway whose parser can change without a commit
  (b) pin the digest AND create a recurring review obligation - explicit, auditable, but needs someone to actually do it
  (c) leave it, and record that the freeze is deliberate and node-lifecycle-bound
Pick one on the merits rather than leaving it implicit.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE AFTER a7n: docker-entrypoint.sh in the nginx image runs under `set -e`, so a non-zero exit from any /docker-entrypoint.d script KILLS the container. a7n added readOnlyRootFilesystem. So a future 1.27-alpine push that adds an entrypoint script WITHOUT a read-only guard now CRASH-LOOPS the internet-facing gateway, where before it would merely have written a stray file. Whichever option is chosen should account for that: (a) makes it reachable without a commit, (b) and (c) make it reachable only on a deliberate change or a node replacement.
Note the same question applies to the other non-${REGISTRY} images - postgres:16-alpine, quay.io/oauth2-proxy:v7.14.3, google/cloud-sdk:slim - though none of them is internet-facing.

title: Bound proxy_max_temp_file_size, then pick an emptyDir sizeLimit for auth-gateway
description:
Filed from genetics-results-suite-o5i, which DECLINED to set a sizeLimit on auth-gateway's `cache` and `tmp` emptyDirs and wrote the reasoning into the manifest. This bead is the prerequisite work that would make a number choosable.

WHY IT WAS DECLINED, arithmetic re-derived against the RENDERED config by two agents: a sizeLimit does not give nginx ENOSPC - the KUBELET EVICTS THE POD. auth-gateway is replicas 1 and internet-facing, so every number buys a disk-fill defence at the price of a new whole-site outage path.
  worker_processes 1, worker_connections 1024, client_max_body_size 50M at HTTP level (so it applies everywhere) -> 51.2 GB of client_temp in the worst case
  proxy_max_temp_file_size NEVER SET, so the 1024m per-request default stands on every buffered location -> another 1 TiB
  proxy_buffering off ONLY on `= /mcp` and `/chat/v1/`; /api/, /status and / all buffer
  both client_temp and proxy_temp land in the SAME volume (/var/cache/nginx)
  node allocatable ephemeral storage: 47,060,071,478 B = 43.83 GiB
So the config's own ceiling is roughly 24x the entire disk and NO number derived from it bounds the adversarial case. Meanwhile 1Gi - the obvious guess - is exactly ONE buffered /api/ response, and /api/ proxies results-api through the BFF with buffering on and 300s timeouts, so a single slow client pulling a large summary-stats range would reach it. 1Gi trades a hypothetical fill for a reachable eviction.

THE PREREQUISITE: bound proxy_max_temp_file_size in the nginx config. That is a BEHAVIOUR change, not a limit - it makes nginx stop buffering to disk past the bound and stream instead (or fail, depending on configuration), so it needs its own traffic test against the real rendered config. The harness shape is recorded in the close reasons of genetics-results-suite-eau, a7n and o5i: extract data["nginx.conf"], render through deploy.sh's envsubst with BOTH fragments populated, stub all eight cluster-local upstreams with --add-host, and drive real traffic including a 20 MB POST and a slow-client 20 MB response.
Once bounded, the worst case becomes computable and a sizeLimit follows.

ALSO WORTH SETTLING: the pod sets no ephemeral-storage request or limit. o5i's comment argued that absence is itself a mitigation, since DiskPressure eviction ranks by usage-above-request. Review correctly weakened that - THE CLUSTER IS A SINGLE NODE, so DiskPressure is cluster-wide, every other workload feels it before the ranking rescues anything, and the evicted pod reschedules onto the same full node. An explicit ephemeral-storage request/limit may be the better instrument than a volume sizeLimit; consider both.

title: Five workloads still mount the default ServiceAccount token
description:
Found while doing genetics-results-suite-o5i, which removed the automounted default ServiceAccount token from auth-gateway. Reported there, deliberately not changed.

RE-DERIVED TWICE, independently, over every pod-template-carrying kind in k8s/ INCLUDING k8s/cronjobs/: 14 workloads total (13 Deployments + 1 CronJob). 8 set serviceAccountName: genetics-suite (monitor-cronjob, mcp-server, analyze-conversations-cronjob, keycloak-postgres-backup, chat-backend, results-api, rag-service, db-api). 1 sets automountServiceAccountToken: false (auth-gateway, as of o5i). FIVE set NEITHER and therefore mount the genetics namespace's `default` token:
  bff, frontend, keycloak, oauth2-proxy, and postgres.yaml (object name keycloak-postgres)
8 + 1 + 5 = 14.

WHAT THE TOKEN IS ACTUALLY WORTH, measured during o5i so it does not need re-deriving: 151 RoleBindings and ClusterRoleBindings scanned, NOT ONE names genetics:default; the ServiceAccount has no iam.gke.io/gcp-service-account annotation so it reaches GCP not at all; its entire authorisation is what any authenticated identity inherits - self-reviews, API discovery, healthz, the OIDC discovery doc. So this is reconnaissance-grade, not escalation - the same honest framing o5i landed on. The value is denying a valid cluster credential and pre-empting the blast radius of any binding someone later grants `default`, which would arrive without anyone rechecking these pods.

NONE IS INTERNET-FACING (auth-gateway, which is, was done in o5i). bff and frontend sit directly behind it, so they are the two worth doing first.

WORK: add automountServiceAccountToken: false to each. Prove per workload that it is functionally inert - none of these should make API-server calls, but VERIFY rather than assume, particularly for oauth2-proxy and keycloak, which are third-party and could plausibly use in-cluster discovery. o5i's approach is the model: run the workload with and without the token directory present and compare behaviour, rather than reasoning from the docs.

WATCH OUT - THIS TRIPPED THE DEPLOY IN o5i: scripts/test-network-policies.py used to treat automountServiceAccountToken: false as a sandbox-only tell, and deploy.sh exits on its failure, mid-deploy, after configs/secrets/PVCs/ingress are applied. o5i REMOVED that tell, so this bead should be clear - but re-run the harness after each change rather than trusting that.

RELATED: genetics-results-suite-d6n covers the eight workloads with no container securityContext, which overlaps this set. Doing them together is probably right, but d6n's own note warns that frontend and oauth2-proxy need a live smoke test.

title: Nothing detects a ${...} placeholder reappearing in auth-gateway.yaml's comments
description:
Filed off genetics-results-suite-i5v, where the fix was a rewording and the reviewer correctly noted it is only as durable as the next editor's care.

THE PROBLEM i5v FIXED: scripts/deploy.sh envsubsts the WHOLE k8s/deployments/auth-gateway.yaml, and two comment regions in that file spelled ${LEGACY_REDIRECT} / ${KEYCLOAK_SERVER} literally. Both fragments are multi-line when populated, so the substitution broke out of the `#` comment and the render stopped being valid YAML - kubectl apply would have failed. Reproduced, fixed, verified.

WHY IT NEEDS A MECHANICAL GUARD: the fix is a convention, enforced only by an invariant comment in the file ("never spell a whitelisted name as ${...} here"). Nothing detects a violation. And the class is not hypothetical - it went unnoticed for as long as it did precisely because NOBODY HAS EVER DRIVEN THIS FILE THROUGH deploy.sh WITH BOTH FRAGMENTS POPULATED. On the current profile both are empty, so the render is well-formed and the bug is invisible. Note it is not daly-only: LEGACY_REDIRECT comes from redirect_from_host/redirect_to_host, which have no profile coupling, so a finngen deploy configuring a legacy redirect hits it too.

WORK: add a check that renders auth-gateway.yaml exactly as deploy.sh:442 does - same shell-format whitelist, same sed - with BOTH fragments populated using the verbatim printf -v forms from deploy.sh:132 and :163, and parses the result as YAML. It should also assert that ${INTERNAL_API_SECRET} survives UNEXPANDED (it is deliberately not whitelisted, because the initContainer substitutes it later - if it ever expanded, the secret would be baked into a ConfigMap) and that nginx's own $host/$remote_addr/$scheme/$request_uri are intact.

WHERE TO PUT IT, decide on the merits: the repo has NO CI except genetics-results-browser's, so the realistic homes are the tracked pre-commit hook (.beads/hooks/pre-commit, where check-doc-drift.sh already lives - note that hook warns and never blocks, and is only wired up by scripts/install-git-hooks.sh) or a deploy.sh preflight next to the existing --check calls. A deploy.sh preflight catches it at the moment it would break; a pre-commit hook catches it earlier but only for people who ran the installer.

The i5v close reason records the exact harness shape, and the alternative fix that was rejected (narrowing envsubst to the nginx.conf value, which needs a YAML-aware tool that preserves block-scalar indentation) is still available if a check proves awkward.

title: tfvars sed uses GNU-only \s, and build.sh warns about nothing from a worktree
description:
Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-1xp; pre-existing, left untouched there deliberately.

TWO SMALL PORTABILITY/DIAGNOSTIC GAPS in the tfvars-parsing scripts, both non-urgent:

1. `\s` IS A GNU SED EXTENSION. scripts/deploy.sh:39, scripts/create-secrets.sh, scripts/build.sh and scripts/build-all.sh all extract tfvars values with `sed 's/.*=\s*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/'`. BSD/macOS sed does not understand `\s`, so the substitution simply does not match and the variable comes back as the WHOLE LINE rather than the value - silently, with exit 0. On Linux this never fires, which is why it has never been noticed. Fix is `[[:space:]]*`, which is POSIX and works on both. Four call sites, one spelling.
   Not urgent: everything today runs on Linux. It matters the first time someone runs deploy.sh or build.sh from a Mac.

2. scripts/build.sh DOES NOT CALL check-worktree-paths.sh, while scripts/build-all.sh:25 does. After 1xp, a build from a worktree with no terraform.tfvars falls back to APP_NAME=FinnGenie - correct behaviour, but with NO warning at all when a single service is built directly. build-all.sh warns; build.sh does not. Decide whether build.sh should get the same preflight call or whether single-service builds are deliberately quieter.

RELATED, DECIDED AND ACCEPTED IN 1xp, recorded so it is not rediscovered as a bug: an UNREADABLE (chmod 000) tfvars is now masked by `|| true` into the FinnGenie fallback with exit 0 and no message. Measured. On daly that bakes the wrong brand into images. Accepted because the prior behaviour on that exact path was a silent exit 2, which is not better - but if a third case ever needs handling here, this is the one to revisit.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 0d804a0. Batched with genetics-results-suite-i5v.

PART A. `\s` converted to [[:space:]] at all four tfvars extraction sites: deploy.sh:32, create-secrets.sh:44, build.sh:23, build-all.sh:31.

SCOPE EXTENSION BEYOND THE BEAD'S LETTER, flagged rather than slipped in and endorsed by review: each of those lines ALSO feeds its sed from a `grep -E '^\s*<key>\s*='` carrying the same GNU-only `\s`. Fixing only the seds would have swapped a WRONG value for an EMPTY one on BSD rather than fixing anything. Both converted.

VERIFIED IDENTICAL ON GNU across SIXTEEN tfvars line shapes, old pair vs new pair, byte for byte: plain, extra spaces, tabs, no spaces around =, a trailing comment containing quotes, a commented-out `# config_profile = ...` line above the real one, commented-out only, CRLF, CRLF+tabs, vertical tab, form feed, NBSP, missing quotes, empty file, and the substring trap `config_profile_override` both alongside the real key and alone. This mattered because deploy.sh:32 derives the profile for the ENTIRE deploy and a misderivation ships the wrong per-profile config. The substring trap does not fire in either version: [[:space:]]*= after the key rejects config_profile_override because `_` is neither space nor `=`.
Character-class membership measured directly under LANG=C.UTF-8: `\s` and [[:space:]] match identically on space, TAB, VT, FF and CR, and both reject NBSP - so there is no GNU input on which the conversion changes the result. The CRLF case in particular yields the same value under both, because the CR sits after the closing quote and [^"]* never reaches it.
BSD behaviour simulated (reading `\s` as a literal 's'): the old pair returns THE WHOLE LINE with exit 0 - the reported bug - while grep's match count drops to 0. The new pair is unaffected.

PART B. build.sh now calls check-worktree-paths.sh --check || true at line 21, matching build-all.sh:25 in invocation and comment style. After 1xp a single-service build from a worktree fell back to APP_NAME=FinnGenie correctly but with NO warning at all; build-all.sh warned and build.sh did not.
The `|| true` is LOAD-BEARING, not decorative: build.sh:2 is `set -euo pipefail` and the preflight genuinely exits 1 in this worktree (measured, 43 ms, with </dev/null). SCRIPT_DIR is defined at line 17, before the call. The preflight only runs git config / git rev-parse / cmp, so it cannot prompt or hang. Verified end to end from this worktree with stub docker/kubectl/gcloud: the warning prints and execution continues well past it.
Checked for a noise regression too - nothing invokes build.sh programmatically (build-all.sh only mentions it in comments, rollout.sh not at all), so the warning cannot fire once per service.
Deliberately did NOT also add install-git-hooks.sh --check to build.sh: that is a separate preflight outside the ruling, and README's claim that only deploy.sh and build-all.sh run it stays true.

REVIEW CAUGHT THE CHANGE FALSIFYING AN EXECUTABLE'S OWN OUTPUT: check-worktree-paths.sh:107-108 told the operator that "build.sh/build-all.sh just silently fall back to APP_NAME=FinnGenie" - and that message IS now the warning build.sh prints, so it was asserting its own absence. Corrected. The two docs that enumerated two callers were corrected to three (deploy.sh:24, build-all.sh:25, build.sh:21), re-derived by grep across the whole repo including .github.
bash -n clean on all four modified scripts.

title: Four SDK functions still lose their schema on an empty result; their endpoints do not stream a TSV
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-6uk, which fixed 12 of the 16 exposed SDK functions and deliberately left these four.

6uk made results-api advertise a JSON range response's columns in an X-Columns header, which the SDK consumes so an empty result keeps its column names. That works because those endpoints STREAM A TSV and range_response can read the file's own header line - even for a zero-row file.

These four do not:
  gene_burden / get_gene_based_results  (app/routers/gene_based.py)
  gene_annotations                      (app/routers/genes.py, gene_groups.py)
  gene_disease                          (app/routers/gene_disease.py)
  search                                (app/routers/search.py)
Their endpoints COMPUTE JSON and return StreamingResponse/TimedJSONResponse directly, never passing through range_response, so there is no file header to advertise. They degrade to a bare pl.DataFrame() - no regression, and 6uk pinned that degradation with a test so an absent header can never raise something new.

WHY THIS IS A DIFFERENT SHAPE OF WORK: fixing them means each router DECLARING its own output columns, rather than reading them off a file. That is the option (b) 6uk rejected for the streaming endpoints, and the reason it was rejected there does not apply here - there is no file header to be a superset of, so a declared list IS the ground truth. But it means a hand-maintained list per router, which is exactly the thing that rots. Whatever is chosen needs a check that fails closed when a router's declared columns and its actual output disagree - see 4h6.31 for the pattern (a generator that REFUSES rather than degrading, plus a test that mutation-proves the refusal).

Do not just hardcode the lists. 4h6.25 rejected a hand-copied schema across a repo boundary and 6uk rejected a generated superset; a third variant with no check would be worse than either.

Low priority: the failure is a script getting a bare empty frame and having to guess column names, which costs a retry iteration rather than producing a wrong answer.

title: The sandbox tracker bound and pod-wide concurrency limit are cross-tenant denial surfaces
description:
Found by a blind validator during genetics-results-suite-4h6.29; documented there, not fixed.

Two of results-api's new limits deny service to OTHER executions rather than only to the caller that exceeded them:

1. SANDBOX_MAX_TRACKED_EXECUTIONS (4096). The accounting map is global and entries are created by ANY valid token, living up to one token lifetime (~305s). A caller able to start 4096 executions inside that window locks out every other user's NEW execution with sandbox_execution_tracker_full. The module argues 23 chat turns/hour makes this unreachable - that is a statement about honest VOLUME, not a bound on an attacker.
   Note this is the direct cost of the (correct) fail-closed eviction choice: because a live entry is never evicted, a full map must refuse newcomers.

2. SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS_TOTAL (8) against SANDBOX_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS (4) means TWO misbehaving executions can deny every other execution pod-wide. Moot while the sandbox is concurrency: 1 - the per-jti limit binds first - but it becomes live the moment sandbox concurrency is raised, which is precisely the scenario the pod-wide limit was added for.

RELATED AND COMPOUNDING: there is no request timeout anywhere (none in run_server.py's uvicorn.run, none in the manifest). A request hung in a GCS read holds a per-execution slot, a pod-wide slot, AND pins its map entry permanently, because _sweep_locked refuses to evict anything with in_flight > 0. So the anti-eviction rule that closes the fail-open direction has no counterpart bounding how long an entry may stay unevictable. A handful of hung requests is enough to reach case 2 without any attacker.

TO DO, roughly in order:
1. Add a request timeout, which is worth doing on its own merits and removes the compounding path. Decide where - uvicorn's timeout, an ASGI middleware, or a per-request asyncio deadline - and note that whatever is chosen must still run release() in a finally.
2. Add per-caller fairness to the pod-wide limit, or drop it in favour of a memory-based admission check, so one execution cannot consume every slot.
3. Consider whether tracker-full should shed the OLDEST idle entry rather than refusing the newest - it changes which party is harmed, and the current choice harms the innocent newcomer.
4. Emit a metric or ERROR log on tracker-full and on pod-wide rejection. Today only logger.warning fires on rejection and nothing logs admissions, so an operator cannot tell a denial from quiet traffic, nor tune 1000/4/8 from production data.

Not urgent: production impact is nil until the sandbox is deployed. Do it in the same window as genetics-results-suite-4h6.7.

title: check-doc-drift.sh's sandbox mapping fires on generated schema docs, where it cannot apply
description:
Observed firing on suite 74bfc7f (genetics-results-suite-4h6.31), which regenerated sandbox/schema/*.md to add a column-type column.

SANDBOX_PATHS in scripts/check-doc-drift.sh is '^(sandbox/|k8s/deployments/sandbox\.yaml$|k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy\.yaml$)' and maps to docs/code-execution-security.md, whose listed concerns are "isolation boundary, egress+ingress allow-lists, the three MCP-exclusion layers, sandbox token claims".

sandbox/schema/*.md are GENERATED schema documentation. They cannot affect any of those four things, so the warning can never apply to them - yet it fires on every regeneration, and the schema docs are regenerated whenever a dataset or column changes, which is often.

WHY THIS MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING TIDY-UP: a warning that fires when it cannot apply is how the check teaches people to ignore it. That is the same failure mode fixed in genetics-results-suite-0xs, where a preflight's beads detection fired in every worktree regardless of staleness and would have turned a four-item check into wallpaper. This check is warn-only, so the cost of ignoring it is exactly the cost of the drift it exists to catch.

FIX: narrow the code-execution-security.md mapping to the paths that can actually change the isolation boundary - the sandbox image, its Dockerfile and entrypoint, k8s/deployments/sandbox.yaml, k8s/network-policies/sandbox-policy.yaml - and exclude sandbox/schema/. Decide separately whether sandbox/schema/ should still map to docs/project-spec.md; it plausibly should, since the spec summarises what the sandbox exposes.

CHECK THE OTHER MAPPINGS FOR THE SAME SHAPE while you are there - any rule whose path pattern is broader than the doc concern it names will do this. The CLAUDE.md ownership table and this script are supposed to mirror each other, so fix both or neither.
close_reason:
Landed as suite 1b1d37b + mcp ae805df. BATCHED: bi1, 5r2, 7zr, fml, dqa in one cycle, per the enumeration-batching rule. FULL tier - test + sighted review + blind validator in parallel, one fix round, then a scoped re-validation. Tests 1370 passed / 74 deselected (baseline exact, module resolution asserted inside the worktree first); ruff check clean. FILE-ONLY: nothing touched the live cluster, BigQuery or any deployed object.

THREE OF THE FIVE BEADS WERE THEMSELVES PARTLY WRONG, which is the headline:
- 7zr item 1 was ALREADY FIXED. auth-gateway.yaml's comment no longer spells ${LEGACY_REDIRECT} literally. The one ${...} left in a comment is INTERNAL_API_SECRET, deliberately absent from deploy.sh's 18-name envsubst whitelist, so it survives verbatim BY DESIGN. No change made.
- 5r2's "bead 4h6.15 names the wrong directory for sandbox_tools.py" was INACCURATE - 4h6.15 never named a directory for that file at all; the real defect was a MISSING path that invited the misreading. 4h6.15's text fixed instead. sandbox_tools.py is at src/genetics_mcp_server/skills/.
- 5r2's "sandbox/** is uncovered in check-doc-drift.sh" was STALE - already covered before this batch. Three more of its items were also already fixed (header scope, the eight-of-fourteen serviceAccountName claim, which re-derives correct).
- bi1 UNDERSTATED item 3: the _reject doc list omitted five of the eight SDK functions' rejections, not just hla()'s.

EVERY NUMBER RE-DERIVED THREE TIMES INDEPENDENTLY - implementer, sighted reviewer, blind validator - and none copied from a doc or a bead: datasets.yaml 15 views, ALL_VIEWS 11, monitor VIEWS 8, api/main.py VIEWS 15, four views outside ALL_VIEWS, mcp api=44 / general=18 / bigquery=2 / orchestration=1, "40 of the 44", 17 _reject sites across 8 functions, 5 count-gated GSA roles, 14 workloads with 8 setting serviceAccountName, e2-standard-2 ~1930m allocatable. The one number that did NOT survive: the "60-tool surface" is 65, and was DROPPED rather than corrected, since a hardcoded count rots again.

VALIDATOR DISAGREEMENTS, resolved empirically rather than averaged:
- Sighted review CLEARED the sandbox exclusion as justified; the BLIND validator falsified it (see dqa's own close reason). Blind was right.
- BOTH validators reported executor.py ~1707-1711 carries a comment whose rationale is false there. The fix agent REFUSED the item and was RIGHT: the comment sits at 1628-1630 above the get_hla_by_allele site, where it is true (that function does echo "resource": resource at 1654); the second site carries no comment. Both validators had conflated adjacent diff hunks. Re-validation confirmed with quoted line numbers.

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS: dqa's requested change was NOT made (its premise is false - see its close reason). bi1 item 2's requested change was NOT made as asked (its suggestion was wrong - see bi1's close reason). bi1's ruff-format question is answered in a separate bead, not decided here.
LEFT ALONE BY MY DECISION: check-doc-drift.sh's scripts/monitor/ -> project-spec mapping has the same over-broad shape dqa complains about (Dockerfile, requirements.txt cannot change the monitored view list), but slack.py CAN change alert behaviour, so it is not clearly a false positive. Not narrowed.

THIS BEAD'S PREMISE IS FALSE AND THE REQUESTED CHANGE IS DELIBERATELY NOT MADE. The bead argued sandbox/schema/*.md are generated docs that "cannot affect" any of the four things docs/code-execution-security.md owns, so the warning can never apply. The doc reasons about the CONTENT of both generated trees:
- :445 the secrets-in-image table names stubs/genetics.pyi and stubs/client.pyi as where INTERNAL_API_SECRET ships, and :452-460 treats that exact wording as an ACCEPTED RESIDUAL;
- :480 and :514-519 state the PLACEHOLDER build gate over BOTH staged schema/ and stubs/;
- :556-575 is an entire section describing what schema/ contains and asserting "neither directory is empty" and that each file carries its description, columns and worked example SQL - all falsifiable by a regeneration.
The stubs really do carry it: sandbox/stubs/client.pyi and genetics.pyi both name INTERNAL_API_SECRET, one citing the doc by name.
MEASURED FAILURE the first round would have shipped: an SDK docstring edit in genetics-mcp-server is baked by gen-sandbox-docs.py into sandbox/stubs/client.pyi, which sandbox/Dockerfile:103 copies verbatim to /genetics/sdk/ where the model reads it. A stubs-only commit - EXACTLY the shape gen-sandbox-docs.py produces - fired NO code-execution-security warning. Found by the blind validator AFTER the sighted reviewer had explicitly checked the exclusions and cleared them as justified.
So the warning dqa calls fatigue is legitimate, and that is now recorded in CLAUDE.md in dqa's own terms rather than left as a rejected ticket.

WHAT DID CHANGE, and it is the more valuable half: the exclusion MECHANISM survives but its contract is narrowed. "Generated by a script" is explicitly no longer accepted as grounds for exemption, since a doc can and does reason about generated content. And the keycloak/themes exemption added in the same round - which the blind validator caught - was directory-shaped and would have SILENCED a keycloak/themes/genetics/login/login.ftl override, a template that changes what the login page lets a user do. Now exemption is by file EXTENSION, verified by running it: login.ftl fires, .css/.png/.woff2 stay silent, exit 0 in every path, and a mixed commit still warns.
The phrase "the four things code-execution-security.md owns" - itself a false enumeration, in the justification for a change about false enumerations - is gone everywhere.
CLAUDE.md's ownership table and the script mirror row-for-row in BOTH directions after this: 8 rows, 8 check calls, one except clause against one script exclusion. (An earlier report said 7 and 7; the count was wrong, the mirroring was not.)

title: db-api reads INTERNAL_API_SECRET at import time, so a module-scope import in any new test breaks test_api_auth
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-tcs, in genetics-results-db.

api/main.py reads INTERNAL_API_SECRET at MODULE IMPORT time. tests/test_api_auth.py sets the env var at FIXTURE time (line 21) and imports api.main at line 23 - but pytest imports every test module during COLLECTION, before any fixture runs. So any future test module that does `from api import main` at module scope freezes INTERNAL_API_SECRET to '' for the whole session and breaks test_api_auth with a failure that points nowhere near the cause.

DEMONSTRATED, not theorised: importing api.main with the env var unset, then setting it and re-importing, leaves INTERNAL_API_SECRET as '' - the module-scope read happens once.

tests/test_endpoint_access_log.py (added by tcs) works around it by importing lazily inside a fixture, with the reason in the fixture docstring. That is a workaround, not a fix, and it only holds as long as every future author notices the docstring.

FIX, pick one:
(a) a conftest.py that sets INTERNAL_API_SECRET before collection - smallest, keeps the module-scope read;
(b) read the secret at REQUEST time rather than import time - removes the global-state hazard entirely and is the honest fix, but touches the auth path, so it needs the same care genetics-results-suite-zyi's compare_digest work did;
(c) leave it and rely on the docstring - not recommended, since the failure mode is a confusing error in an UNRELATED test file.

Prefer (b) if the auth path is being touched anyway; (a) otherwise. Note that whichever is chosen, a test should pin it - the current arrangement passes for a reason no test states.
notes:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 during genetics-results-suite-ctq, and it is WORSE THAN THE DESCRIPTION: this is not only a "new test breaks" hazard, it silently makes NINE EXISTING AUTH TESTS PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON.

db-api's tests are order-dependent under pytest-randomly. With --randomly-seed=2662673150, running tests/test_endpoint_access_log.py BEFORE tests/test_api_auth.py leaves api.main.INTERNAL_API_SECRET as "" - it is read ONCE at import - so require_auth takes its FAIL-OPEN branch and nine auth tests get 200 where they assert 401. Reproduced with the ctq work's new tests deselected, so it is not introduced by that change.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL FRAMING: a green db-api suite is not evidence that the auth path works, because the ordering that exercises it fail-open is reachable by an ordinary shuffled run. Any future change to require_auth could be validated by a suite that never actually tested it.
FIX DIRECTION UNCHANGED (read the secret lazily rather than at import), but add a regression test that pins the fail-open branch as UNREACHABLE when the secret is set, and consider whether the fail-open branch should exist at all outside an explicit dev flag.
SEPARATELY, also found: tests/test_build_phenotypes.py cannot be COLLECTED in the db worktree because scripts/build_phenotypes.py imports fsspec, which is not installed. Pre-existing and unrelated, but it means "the db suite passes" has been measured with that file ignored.

--- CORRECTION 2026-08-13, to the "MEASURED" note above. Two of its claims were wrong. ---

1. THE INVERTED CLAIM. "Silently makes nine existing auth tests PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON" and "a green db-api suite is not evidence that the auth path works" are BACKWARDS. A test that asserts 401 and receives 200 FAILS. Re-measured against the pre-fix api/main.py at --randomly-seed=2662673150: 9 FAILED, 87 passed. The defect was a SEED-DEPENDENT RED SUITE — loud and self-announcing — not a silent green one. The wrong framing was propagated from this note into api/main.py's docstring, both project-spec.md files, pyproject.toml and tests/test_secret_read_timing.py; all corrected in the same change rather than softened.

   The honest justification, which still stands: the auth path's behaviour depended on TEST COLLECTION ORDER, so a shuffled run could go red for reasons unrelated to whatever was being changed, and a future module-scope `import api.main` in any test file would freeze the secret and break an unrelated file (which is the original description's point). Worth fixing; not "auth was never tested".

2. THE fsspec CLAIM IS INTERPRETER-SPECIFIC, not a property of the worktree. tests/test_build_phenotypes.py COLLECTS FINE in the project .venv, which has fsspec 2026.7.0 (148 tests collected, all pass). It fails to collect only under the GLOBAL pyenv interpreter, where fsspec is absent (132 collected + 1 collection error; 132 pass with --ignore=tests/test_build_phenotypes.py). "The db suite passes" measured with that file ignored is therefore a statement about the global interpreter, not about the checkout.

ALSO FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE (both were introduced by the per-request read, i.e. by this bead's fix, and neither is reachable in the deployment):
  * an in-process delete/empty of INTERNAL_API_SECRET after import would have disabled authentication entirely (every request admitted with principal=None) — a safety property the old module global gave for free. _internal_api_secret now LATCHES asymmetrically: runtime changes may ENABLE auth (empty -> set, which the ordering tests need) but never DISABLE it; set -> empty fails CLOSED. Pinned by test_a_configured_process_never_fails_open_afterwards.
  * _require_ascii_secret raising inside the request-time accessor was a 500 for EVERY call, including one holding the correct credential, on a pod kubelet keeps Ready (/health returns before the read) — the inverse of ctq's designed rollout-stalling failure. Startup still raises; request time now fails closed with 401.
  * the env leak was fixed at its source: _reload in tests/test_sandbox_token_auth.py popped INTERNAL_API_SECRET/SANDBOX_TOKEN_SIGNING_KEY/SANDBOX_ENABLED and set PROJECT_ID with nothing restoring them; it now routes all of that through monkeypatch. conftest's restore_auth_env is kept as a net, and its docstring now says so.
  * pytest-randomly was declared but NOT installed in the project .venv (it was only in the global pyenv, which is where the shuffled measurements came from). The venv is now synced with the dev extra; the pyproject comment claiming it "was already installed here and never declared" was false for this checkout and is corrected.
close_reason:
Landed as db 515851c + suite 5ad251f. FULL tier - test + sighted review + blind validator in parallel, one fix round, a scoped re-validation, then a targeted spec fix. 148 passed in the project venv across four orderings, no variation. FILE-ONLY.

I WAS WRONG IN THIS BEAD'S OWN NOTES AND THE ERROR PROPAGATED. My note said the hazard "silently makes NINE EXISTING AUTH TESTS PASS FOR THE WRONG REASON" and that "a green db-api suite is not evidence that the auth path works". THAT IS BACKWARDS - a test asserting 401 that receives 200 FAILS. The blind validator reproduced the old code at seed 2662673150: 9 FAILED / 87 passed, exactly the nine tests named. The real defect is a SEED-DEPENDENT RED SUITE, which is loud and self-announcing, plus the standing hazard that a future module-scope `import api.main` freezes the secret and breaks an unrelated test file. Worth fixing; NOT the emergency the note described. The inverted claim had already propagated into five places (api/main.py's accessor docstring, db docs/project-spec.md, db pyproject.toml's dev-extra comment, and two spots in the new test file) and is corrected in all of them. The sighted reviewer did NOT catch this - it checked whether the change was correct, not whether its justification was true.

SHIPPED: one accessor that reads AND ASCII-validates in the same function, so the value compared is by construction the value validated. The naive form of the bead's option (b) - fresh read, stale snapshot validated - is UNREPRESENTABLE rather than merely avoided, which matters because genetics-results-suite-ctq's latin-1-vs-utf-8 comparison is only well-defined while the secret is ASCII. Option (a), a conftest that sets the var before collection, was rejected: it keeps the module-scope read and only hides the hazard.

TWO SAFETY PROPERTIES THE FIRST DRAFT LOST, both found by the BLIND validator via a 12-case admit/reject matrix run against old and new code, and both restored. The sighted reviewer saw the same facts and returned "no BLOCKING findings"; I overrode that, because both were cheap to restore and one of them was a property I had explicitly required.
1. Deleting or emptying INTERNAL_API_SECRET in-process ADMITTED EVERY REQUEST. The old module global could not be disabled that way. Now the accessor is TRI-STATE (non-empty str authenticates; "" means never-configured and fails open; None means refuse) behind a ONE-WAY LATCH seeded at import and set on any non-empty ASCII read. Runtime changes may ENABLE authentication and may NEVER disable it. require_auth tests `is None` BEFORE the falsiness check that implements fail-open - None is falsy too, and reaching that branch would be a silent total bypass. Re-validation attacked exactly this: 11-case probe against the real app confirms nothing admits with principal=None except /health, and a valid sandbox token still works on a latched process because it returns before the secret read.
2. A non-ASCII secret became a PER-REQUEST 500 on a pod that STAYS READY, because /health returns before the read. That inverts ctq's designed failure mode (rollout stalls, old pods keep serving). Import still crashes; the request path now fails CLOSED with 401. Verified: correct credential + runtime non-ASCII mutation -> 401 with no traceback in the body, and import with a non-ASCII secret still raises RuntimeError.

THE FAIL-OPEN BRANCH IS DELIBERATELY KEPT, against my own earlier suggestion to remove it. A probe established it is documented local-dev behaviour (README:90-93, whose example curls send no header), asserted by name by two tests, and UNREACHABLE in production: non-optional secretKeyRef that deploy.sh gates on and create-secrets.sh always populates, ClusterIP with no Ingress, NetworkPolicy admitting only chat-backend/mcp-server/sandbox - and the sandbox, the one attacker-authored caller, is routed and hard-401'd BEFORE that branch. Removing it is a behaviour and docs change beyond this ticket.

TEST-SIDE, and this is the part that was nearly shipped as a workaround. The first draft added a blanket autouse conftest fixture restoring three env vars. It was load-bearing - without it two tests fail - but the ACTUAL fault was tests/test_sandbox_token_auth.py's _reload popping INTERNAL_API_SECRET and never restoring it, pulling the secret out from under a module-scoped TestClient its own siblings share. That is the same order dependence RELOCATED from module globals into the process environment. Fixed at the source: _reload now routes through monkeypatch, PROJECT_ID included, across eight call sites in four files. PROVEN at source rather than double-netted - re-validation neutralised the conftest net with a plugin and the suite still passed 148 in three orderings. The net is kept as defence in depth and its docstring now says plainly it is a net, not the fix.
NEW TESTS ARE NON-VACUOUS, established twice: 2 of the original 4 fail against HEAD's api/main.py for the right reasons (the other 2 are declared controls), and a mutation harness that reinstalls a naive os.environ.get accessor turns three tests RED.

pytest-randomly DECLARED (authorised scope extension). It was never in this project's venv - the shuffled measurements all came from a global pyenv interpreter - so nobody following the README was exercising the order independence this bead is about. A validator ran `uv sync --extra dev` in the shared worktree DURING review, which changed the venv; that was established and normalised rather than left ambiguous.
uv.lock is UNTRACKED and left unstaged. Recommendation recorded (track it - the sibling repos do, and the dev extra now determines whether the suite shuffles, so an unpinned resolution changes HOW the tests run), but it is the user's call.

CORRECTION TO A SEPARATE CLAIM IN THESE NOTES: "tests/test_build_phenotypes.py cannot be COLLECTED in the db worktree" is INTERPRETER-SPECIFIC, not a property of the worktree. The project venv has fsspec and collects it (148 tests); the global pyenv interpreter does not and needs --ignore (132). The venv is authoritative - it is what README tells you to build and the only one whose plugin set matches pyproject.toml.

FILED: genetics-results-suite-<sandbox bead> for the same import-time-snapshot hazard remaining in api/sandbox_auth.py. Batched nits appended to genetics-results-suite-e8e.

title: check-doc-drift.sh cannot detect enumeration rot, which is what every drift found so far actually was
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-rxw, which established the limitation while fixing a different half of the problem.

scripts/check-doc-drift.sh warns when a changed PATH has a mapped DOC that was not changed in the same commit. That is all it does. It cannot detect the failure mode CLAUDE.md actually warns about:

  "A doc is stale the moment it ENUMERATES something the code no longer matches.
   Counts and lists rot silently - view lists, endpoint tables, env-var tables,
   service inventories - so re-derive them from the code rather than trusting them."

EVERY drift this epic has found was enumeration rot, not a missing doc update:
- docs/project-spec.md asserted a node-pool pinning that was never applied
- surge arithmetic (3951m / 13.60 GiB from a '2651m / 7.91 GiB steady state') that no profile has ever produced
- the datasets/phenotypes docs carried a stale ~33k row count
- the ALL_VIEWS list was one short
- genetics-results-suite-eau (2026-08-11) replaced a rotted 'every application container sets ...' claim with an explicit enumeration THAT WAS WRONG ON DAY ONE - it missed k8s/cronjobs/keycloak-postgres-backup.yaml - and shipped a self-check instruction (`grep k8s/deployments/`) that by construction could not see the directory the missed file was in
- genetics-results-suite-re3 (2026-08-11) had two investigations cite a BigQuery table that turned out to be a different machine's log

The eau case is the sharpest evidence: a human-written enumeration and its own re-derivation instruction were BOTH wrong at the moment of writing, and the doc-drift hook fired correctly on that commit while being structurally incapable of noticing.

WHAT A CHECK COULD ACTUALLY DO, roughly in order of value for effort:
1. Assert that named inventories match a derivable source. Start with the ones that have rotted: the container-hardening lists in project-spec/README vs `grep -rn allowPrivilegeEscalation k8s/` PLUS the complement of the workload inventory; ALL_VIEWS vs configs/datasets.yaml; the service table vs k8s/deployments/*.
2. Assert that any fenced code block or table cell claiming to be a command's OUTPUT can be regenerated and still matches.
3. Fail on a doc that cites a BigQuery table, k8s object or file path that does not exist.

Note (1) is the only one that addresses the actual hit rate, and it needs each enumeration to declare its source - e.g. an HTML comment marking the block and the command that regenerates it. That is a real design task, not a grep.

DECIDE FIRST whether this is worth building or whether the discipline belongs in review instead. The honest counter-argument: every instance above was caught by a human or an agent reading carefully, not by tooling, and a check that covers three enumerations while the docs contain fifty may create false confidence in the other forty-seven. If it is built, it should say plainly which enumerations it covers.

RELATED, unresolved and the user's call: whether check-doc-drift.sh should block rather than warn. Recorded in rxw's description; the warning does get seen, so blocking may not be the lever.
notes:
RELATED: genetics-results-suite-lxz - configs/datasets.yaml has no entry for peak_to_gene_v, while ALL_VIEWS includes it and a credible_sets_v worked example references it. Live BigQuery has 18 tables / 15 views; ALL_VIEWS(11)+2 metadata = 13; datasets.yaml describes 12. The three lists reconcile with nothing. Worth doing in the same pass as this bead.

CORRECTION 2026-08-13: an earlier note here linked genetics-results-suite-lxz, claiming configs/datasets.yaml had no entry for peak_to_gene_v. THAT WAS FALSE and lxz is withdrawn - datasets.yaml has all 15 views including peak_to_gene_v (line 1412), gene_annotations_v and variant_annotation_v. The real and still-open discrepancy is only this: live BigQuery has 15 views and datasets.yaml describes all 15, but ALL_VIEWS (genetics-results-db/scripts/generate_resource_sql.py:22-34) has 11, omitting gene_annotations_v and variant_annotation_v. Whether that omission is deliberate is exactly what this bead is for.

FOUND 2026-08-13 during the fml/5r2/7zr/bi1/dqa doc-accuracy batch, and it belongs here because the fix is a new rule rather than a corrected one:

scripts/gen-sandbox-docs.py, scripts/test-sandbox-docs.py and scripts/test-network-policies.py appear in NO row of CLAUDE.md's ownership table. gen-sandbox-docs.py in particular OWNS THE SANDBOX SCHEMA-DOC CONTRACT - it is the script whose output docs/code-execution-security.md makes falsifiable claims about (that neither generated directory is empty, that the PLACEHOLDER files are gone, that each file carries its description, columns and worked example SQL). A change to the generator can invalidate all of those with no path-based warning at all, because the generator is not a mapped path.

This is the same gap from the other direction: that batch established that the GENERATED TREES must stay mapped (the exemption for them was reverted as unsound). The GENERATOR still is not.

Also relevant to this bead's design: gen-sandbox-docs.py's _sync() only manages .md/.pyi suffixes, so a hand-added file under sandbox/schema/ or sandbox/stubs/ is neither swept as stale nor distinguishable from generated content. Any "is this generated?" check this bead designs cannot rely on the directory alone.

title: Eight workloads still have no container securityContext
description:
Split out of genetics-results-suite-eau, which hardened auth-gateway and enumerated the rest rather than fixing them.

Re-derived from k8s/ twice during eau, so this list is current as of suite 13f074c:
  Deployments: frontend, oauth2-proxy, keycloak, postgres, rag-service
  CronJobs:    monitor (pod-level fsGroup: 1000 only), analyze-conversations, keycloak-postgres-backup (k8s/cronjobs/)
None sets a container-level securityContext. The only other securityContext hits in the tree are pod-level fsGroup at chat-backend.yaml:24 and monitor-cronjob.yaml:19, which is not hardening.

DO NOT DO THESE AS ONE CHANGE. eau proved the failure mode: a bare capabilities.drop: [ALL] would have CrashLooped the internet-facing gateway, for a reason the bead had not anticipated (the image's root master chowns temp paths and setuids its workers). Each image needs the same empirical treatment - run it locally under docker with --cap-drop=ALL --security-opt=no-new-privileges against its real config, and find out what it actually needs before shipping a drop.

Prioritise by exposure: oauth2-proxy sits in the request path; postgres and keycloak hold credentials; rag-service and frontend are lower; the three CronJobs are lowest but keycloak-postgres-backup runs google/cloud-sdk:slim with a Postgres password from keycloak-secrets.

Expect the same trap eau hit twice: several of these images run a root process that drops to a service user, so drop-ALL alone breaks them and the honest fix is runAsUser plus writable-dir emptyDirs rather than capability juggling. Also expect the docs to need updating in the same commit - docs/project-spec.md and README.md both ENUMERATE this list, and docs/code-execution-security.md defines a 'suite baseline' term that these workloads are explicitly outside of.

title: results-api logs no response size, so the endpoint_access sink can never answer size questions
description:
Found while validating genetics-results-suite-re3, and it corrects a premise that bead inherited.

re3 said httpRequest.responseSize was 'non-null on 0 of 2,812 rows', implying the sink drops it. It was never there to drop. MEASURED: httpRequest is NULL on all 278,757 rows across BOTH tables in genetics_api_logs. genetics-results-api/app/middleware_usage_logging.py calls logger.info() with a plain dict, which produces a jsonPayload-only entry; Cloud Logging populates the httpRequest struct only when a caller sets it, and nothing here does. The column exists in the schema because the Logging export schema is fixed, not because anything writes it.

So no sink configuration change can produce response sizes. It needs a middleware change.

WHY IT MATTERS: docs/code-execution-security.md's truncation analysis wanted exactly this data and had to fall back to reasoning about caps instead of measuring. That fallback is sound (see the code-execution-security re-measurement bead) but it means the question 'has any response ever approached the cap' is currently unanswerable from logs.

TO DO (sibling repo genetics-results-api):
Add a response_bytes field to the endpoint_access payload in app/middleware_usage_logging.py - capture Content-Length where present, or accumulate body bytes in the send wrapper for streaming responses. Note that most of results-api's large responses ARE streaming (TimedStreamingResponse), so Content-Length alone will miss precisely the cases the size question is about.
Then update this repo's docs/project-spec.md log-sinks bullet, which currently states that httpRequest is never populated.

Low priority: nothing is broken, a capability is simply absent. Raise it if the truncation question comes up again.

title: mcp_server.py query_string.decode() has the same undecodable-bytes 500 as the bearer header
description: Found while fixing genetics-results-suite-zyi's fourth compare_digest instance, deliberately left out of that change as out of scope. genetics-mcp-server src/genetics_mcp_server/mcp_server.py ~line 349, the MCP_ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN branch, does query_string.decode() with no guard. A non-UTF-8 query string raises UnicodeDecodeError inside raw ASGI middleware, where there is nothing above it to turn the exception into a response, so the caller gets a bare 500 instead of a 401. This is the identical shape just fixed on the same file's authorization-header decode (~line 335), which is now wrapped in try/except UnicodeDecodeError falling through to the existing 401 branch. NOT REACHABLE BY DEFAULT: the branch is gated on MCP_ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN, which is unset in every k8s manifest and script in the suite, so this is latent unless someone enables query-token auth. Note that 'latent' was ALSO claimed of the zyi bug and turned out to be false, so verify the gating rather than trusting this description. FIX: same treatment as the header decode, plus a test sending a non-UTF-8 query string through the hand-built ASGI scope in tests/test_mcp_server.py's TestBearerAuthMiddleware (which is how the two new bearer tests avoid httpx refusing to encode non-ASCII values).
close_reason:
Landed with genetics-results-suite-ctq (mcp-server 23f42ae). See ctq's close reason for the shared validation.

Now wrapped in try/except UnicodeDecodeError setting query_string = "", matching the header-decode fix on the same file ~15 lines above.
Traced rather than assumed: "" -> parse_qs -> {} -> token None -> the `if token and ...` guard is False -> await _send_401 and return. It reaches the EXISTING 401 with no fallthrough to the inner app.

THE BEAD WARNED THAT "LATENT" HAD BEEN CLAIMED OF THE PREDECESSOR (zyi) AND WAS FALSE, so the gating was verified AGAINST THE LIVE CLUSTER rather than against the manifests: MCP_ALLOW_QUERY_TOKEN is absent from all 18 explicit env vars on the deployed mcp-server, and the only envFrom is ConfigMap bearer-auth-allowed, whose keys are exactly ALLOWED_EMAILS, ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS and GOOGLE_TOKEN_AUDIENCE. Without the fix the decode raises and the test errors. It asserts both call_log == [] and a 401.
